definition: and ↓ suqaAyapN and ↓ masoqaApN and ↓ misoqaApN A place for giving to drink or for watering: (K, * TA:) what is termed siqaAyapu AlmaA='i is well known: (S:) i.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ suqaAyapN and ↓ masoqaApN and ↓ misoqaApN A place for giving to drink or for watering: (K, * TA:) what is termed siqaAyapu AlmaA='i is well known: (S:) i. e. siqaAyapN signifies a place made, or prepared, for the giving to drink to people: (Msb:) a construction for water: (Mgh:) or a place in which beverage is made, or prepared, at the fairs, or festivals, &c.: (JK, T, TA:) [and particularly a place in which a beverage made of raisins steeped in water was given at the general assembly of the pilgrims: ] and ↓ masoqaApN signifies a drinkingplace [in a general sense]: and he who pronounces it with kesr to the m [↓ misoqaApN ] makes it to be like the utensil called misoqaApu Ald~iyki [ the drinking-vessel of the cock ]: (S:) [see turofapN :] and the pl. is masaAqK . (TA.) ― -b2- siqaAyapN also signifies A vessel in which one is given to drink: (K:) in the Kur [xii. 70], it means the king's drinking-cup; (Mgh;) his SuwaAE , in [or from ] which he drank, (JK, S, TA,) and with which they measured corn; and it was a vessel of silver. (TA.) ― -b3- And siqaAyapu AlHaAji means The beverage made of raisins steeped in water which [ the tribe of ] Kureysh used to give to the pilgrims to drink: it was under the superintendence of El-'Abbás in the Time of Ignorance and in El-Islám: (TA:) or siqaAyap in this phrase is an inf. n.; so in the Kur ix. 19; (Mgh;) where it is said, A^ajaEalotumo siqaAyapa A@loHaAji waEimaArapaA@lomasojidi A@loHaraAmi kamano A=mana biA=ll~`hi waA@lyawomi A@loA=xiri ; the two words sqAyp and EmArp being inf. ns. of saqaY and Eamara ; (Bd;) the meaning being A^ajaEalotumo A^ahola siqaAyapi AlHaAji wa EimaArapi Almasojidi AlHaraAmi [i. e. definition: The roof of a house, or chamber: (S, Mgh, * K: *) or the interior uppermost part [i.
sourceDefinition: The roof of a house, or chamber: (S, Mgh, * K: *) or the interior uppermost part [i. e. the ceiling ] of a house, or chamber; the exterior uppermost part thereof being called SahowapN : (Ham p. 725:) or [the height ] from the top to the bottom of a house or chamber. (K.) [And hence, The canopy of the heaven or sky: or] the measure of the height of the heaven from the earth: or the thickness thereof, upwards. (Bd in lxxix. 28.) And The stature, or height in a standing posture, or anything: (K:) thus expl. by Lth: one says biEiyrN Tawiylu Als~amoki [ A camel tall of stature ]. (TA.) [In the present day, it signifies The extent of anything from top to bottom; its height, depth, and thickness: and is vulgarly pronounced sumok .]

sourceDefinition: Fish; syn. HuwtN ; (K;) a kind of aquatic creatures: [a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. with p : pl. of the former simaAkN and sumuwkN . (S, TA.) $awaY fiY AlHariyqi samakatahu [ He broiled his fish in the fire of a burning house ] is a post-classical prov. of the people of Baghdád, relating to the concealing, disguising, or cloaking, of a fault, for the purpose of seizing an opportunity; orginating from the fact that the thief used, when he saw the fire of a burning house in a place, to go thither for the purpose of theft; and if it were in his power, he did what he desired; and if he were lighted on, he said, I came to broil a fish. (Mtr, in Har pp. 481-2.) ― -b2- Als~amakapu [is a name of (tropical:) The constellation Pisces; also called Als~amakataAni ;] a certain sign of the Zodiac; (K, TA;) thought by ISd to be so called because it is a watery sign; and also called AlHuwtu . (TA.)

definition: A thing with which a thing is raised, elevated, upraised, or uplifted;
sourceDefinition: A thing with which a thing is raised, elevated, upraised, or uplifted; (K, TA;) whether a wall or a roof: (TA:) pl. sumukN . (K.) -A2- Als~imaAkaAni is the name of Two bright stars; Als~imaAku AlA^aEozalu and Als~imaAku Alr~aAmiHu : (S, O, K:) the former is a star [namely a ] in Virgo, called by astrologers Als~unobulapu [or Spica Virginis ]; (Kzw;) and is one of the Mansions of the Moon, (S, O, and Kzw in his descr. of the Mansions of the Moon,) the Fourteenth thereof; (Kzw ibid.;) it is one of the A^anowaA=' [pl. of nawo'N , q. v.], and rises aurorally in ti$oriynu AlA^aw~alu [ October, O. S.; its auroral rising, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, began on the 4th of that month ]; it is called AlA Ezl because it has no star [near] before it, like the AEzl that has with him no spear; or, as some say, because, when it rises [aurorally], it is not accompanied by wind nor by cold: (TA:) the latter simaAk , i. e. Alr~aAmiHu , [thus called for a reason expl. in art. rmH , q. v., is the star Arcturus, and] is not of the Mansions of the Moon, (S, O, TA,) and has not any nawo' [here meaning supposed influence in bringing rain &c. ]; it is towards the north; the former being towards the south; (TA;) and is also called Als~imaAku Almirozamu : (AZ, TA in art. rmH :) [it is erroneously said that] the smAkAn are in the sign of Libra: (TA:) and it is said that they are the two kind legs of Leo ( rijolaA AlA^asadi ): (S, O, K: *) [for it appears, as I have before observed, (voce *iraAEN ,) that the ancient Arabs, or many of them, extended the figure of Leo (as they did also that of Scorpio) far beyond the limits which we assign to it: and hence,] AlsmAk AlA Ezl was also called saAqu AlA^asadi [ the thigh, or the hind shank, of Leo ]. (Kzw in his descr. of Virgo.) The rhyming-proser says, A_i*aA TalaEa Als~imaAko *ahaba AlEikaAko faA^aSoliHo finaAko waA^ajid~a Hi*aAko faA_in~a Al$~itaA='a qado A^ataAko [ When AlsmAk rises aurorally, (i. e. AlsmAk AlA Ezl ,) the sultriness has gone, therefore do thou put thy court, or yard, in good condition, and renew thy sandal, for the winter has come to thee: finaAk and Hi*aAk being contractions of finaA='ak and Hi*aA='ak , for the sake of the rhyme]. (O, TA.) The nawo' [here app. meaning the rain consequent upon the auroral setting] of AlsmAk AlAEzl [about the 4th of April, O. S. in Central Arabia] is abundant, but disapproved, because it gives growth to the na$or [q. v.], which diseases the camels that pasture upon it. (Kzw in his descr. of the Mansions of the Moon.) [The epithet ↓ simaAkiY~N is applied to the rain above mentioned.] ― -b2- Als~imaAku also signifies, (K,) or simaAku Alt~aroquwapi , (Ibn-'Abbád, O,) The upper part of the chest, next to the collar-bone. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.)

sourceDefinition: , [aor. yasonuw ,] inf. n. sunuw~N and sinaAyapN and sinaAwapN , i. q. saqaY [as meaning He watered, or irrigated, land]. (M.) [Hence,] one says A^aroDN ↓ masonuw~apN and ↓ masoniy~apN , (S, M, K,) meaning Watered, or irrigated, land: (M:) the w in masoniy~apN being changed into Y , (S, M,) in the opinion of Sb, (M,) like as it is in qinoyapN ; (S;) for he knew not sanayotuhaA [as meaning I watered it ], holding masoniy~apN to be from [ sanaAhaA having for its aor.] yasonuwhaA . (M.) One says [also], sanati Aln~aAqapu , aor. tasonuw , (S, K,) inf. n. [as above, or] sinaAwapN and sinaAyapN , (TA,) The she-camel watered, or irrigated, land. (S, K, TA.) And Als~aHaAbapu tasonuw AlA^aroDa (S, Msb) The cloud waters the land. (Msb.) And sanaAka Algayovu (assumed tropical:) [ The rain gave thee water for thy land, or may the rain give thee water ], inf. n. snw and snY [app. sunuw~N and suniY~N ]. (TA.) And Als~aHaAbu yasonuw AlmaTara (assumed tropical:) [ The clouds send down rain ]. (TA.) And sanati Als~aHaAbapu biAlmaTari (assumed tropical:) [ The cloud watered, or irrigated, with rain ], aor. tasonuw and tasoniY . (M, TA.) And sanati Als~amaA='u , aor. tasonuw , inf. n. sunuw~N , (tropical:) The sky rained. (TA.) ― -b2- sanati Ald~aAb~apu , aor. tasoniY ; (M in art. snY ;) or saniyat , (K, * TA,) aor. tasonaY , like taroDaY ; (K, TA;) The beast [by which is app. meant, in the M, the horse, for it is there added wagayoruhaA , meaning that the verb is said in like manner of other animals, which is the case, for it is generally said of a camel,] was used for the drawing of water upon it [to irrigate land: see saAniyapN , below]. (M, K.) And sanaA , aor. yasonuw , said of a beast [turning a water-wheel], He turned round about the well. (R, TA.) And Alqawomu yasonuwna liA^anofusihimo , (S, K,) inf. n. sinaAyapN , and sometimes sAniyapN , (TA,) The people, or party, draw water for themselves; (S, K; [in some copies of the former of which, A_i*aA A^asoqawoA is erroneously put for A_i*aA A@sotaqawoA , the reading in both of my copies;]) and so ↓ AisotanawoA^a lAnfshm . (M, * TA.) And sanaA EalaY AlbaEiyri , inf. n. sanaAyapN [app. a mistranscription for sinaAyapN ], He drew water upon the camel; which camel is termed saAniyapN . (MA.) And baEiyrN yusonaY Ealayohi A camel upon which water is drawn. (Mgh and Msb in explanation of saAniyapN .) And biy^orN yusonaY minohaA [ A well from which water is drawn, app. by means of the camel called saAniyap ]. (M.) And sanawotu Ald~alowa , inf. n. sinaAyapN , I drew the bucket from the well. (TA.) -A2- sanati Aln~aAru , (M, K,) aor. tasonuw , inf. n. sanaA='N , (M,) The fire became high in its light. (M, K.) And sanaA Albaroqu , (M, K,) aor. yasonuw , inf. n. sanaA='N , (TA,) The lightning shone, shone brightly, or gleamed: (M, K, TA:) [or gleamed upwards, or shot up: for, in the Kur xxiv. 43,] some read, yakaAdu sanaA='u baroqihi yadohabu biA@loA^aboSaAri , meaning The rising and gleaming upwards of his lightning [ nearly taketh away the sight, lit. sights ]; others reading sanaA , of which sanaA=' is not a dial. var. (M.) And ↓ AsnY Albaroqu signifies [in like manner] The lightning shone, or gleamed; or diffused itself, and rose. (M.) And sanaA A_ilaY maEaAliY AlA^umuwri (assumed tropical:) He rose [or aspired ] to the means of attaining eminence. (M.) And sanuwa fiY Hasabihi , inf. n. sanaA='N , (assumed tropical:) He became high, or exalted, in his grounds of pretension to respect or honour. (M.) And saniYa , like raDiYa , He (a man, TA) was, or became, high, or exalted, in rank. (K, * TA.) -A3- See also 2, in two places. -A4- And see 5.

definition: He raised, exalted, or elevated, him, or it.
sourceDefinition: He raised, exalted, or elevated, him, or it. (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- AsnY Aln~aAra He raised the light of the fire. (M.) ― -b3- AsnY lahu AljaAy^izapa He raised [ in value ], to him, the jAy^zp [i. e. gift, or present ]. (TA.) And A^asonayonaA lahu AljaEaAlapa We made much and high [ in amount ], to him, the pay. (Har p. 134.) ― -b4- And AsnY jiwaArahu i. q. A^aHosanahu [app. meaning He made good his covenant of protection ]. (TA.) -A2- AsnY Albaroqu The lightning sent its light into the house, or tent, or chamber: or fell upon the ground: or flew along in the clouds; (K, TA;) or, sometimes, elsewhere, not in the clouds: but it is only in the night. (TA.) See also another explanation near the end of the first paragraph. -A3- AsnY Alqawomu , (S, M, K,) inf. n. A_isonaA='N , (S) The people, or party, tarried a year (S, K) in a place: (S:) or it signifies A^ataY Ealayohimu AlEaAmu [ the year passed over them; meaning they remained to the end of the year ]. (M.) But A^asonatuwA signifies They were afflicted with drought, or barrenness: (S, M, * K: [Freytag has erroneously assigned this signification to AisotanawoA :]) the w , (S,) or the Y , which is originally w , (M,) being changed into t , (S, M,) to distinguish between this verb and AsnY in the sense expl. above. (S. [See art. snt .])

definition: Light: (Msb, MF:) or the light of lightning, (S, M, K,) and of fire: (M:) or the point, or extremity, of the light of lightning: (T, TA:) or light shining or gleaming, or diffusing itself and rising:...
sourceDefinition: Light: (Msb, MF:) or the light of lightning, (S, M, K,) and of fire: (M:) or the point, or extremity, of the light of lightning: (T, TA:) or light shining or gleaming, or diffusing itself and rising: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or a high light: and applied also to the shining, or gleaming, of weapons: (Ham p. 271:) MF says that the apparent particularization in the K [&c.] seems to have been taken from the verse of the Kur [xxiv. 43], and that the word is correctly a general term, meaning as expl. in the Msb: (TA:) [it is originally sanawN , though mentioned in the K as belonging to art. snY ; for] the dual is sanawaAni : As knew not a verb belonging to it. (TA.) -A2- Also [The cassia senna of Linn.; the common senna of medicine; so called in the present day; and also called sanaAmak~ap , and sanaA HijaAziY~ ;] a certain plant, (S, M, Msb, K,) used as a medicine; (S, TA;) and recommended in a trad.; (TA;) an attenuant of the yellow bile and the black bile and the phlegm, (K, TA,) howsoever used; (TA;) [and] used as a collyrium; (M;) AHn describes it as a shrub, or small tree, of the [ class called ] A^agolaAv [pl. of galavN ], which is mixed with Hin~aA=' , and improves and strengthens its colour, and blackens it; and which has a fruit of such kind that, when it dries up, and is put in motion by the wind, it causes to be heard a sound such as is termed zajal [q. v.]: (M in arts. snw and snY , and TA:) its name is as above and ↓ sanaA='N : (M, K:) and the n. un. is sanaApN and sanaA='apN : (M in arts. snw and snY :) the dual of sanFA is sanayaAni , and some say sanawaAni . (M in art. snY .) [Accord. to a gloss. in a copy of the S, as stated by Golius, the dual sanawaAni is applied to The leaves of cyprus (or Hin~aA=' ) and senna mixed together, with which the hair is dyed black.] In the phrase sanaA Almisoki , in a verse of El-Jaadee, the plant [above mentioned] may be meant, as though it were mixed with musk: or it may be from sanFA signifying “ light; ” because the diffusion of odour is like that of light. (M.) -A3- sanaA , (JM,) or sanaA sanaA , (TA,) without teshdeed, and also with tesh-deed, to the n , is an Abyssinian expression, meaning Hasuna [q. v.], (JM, TA,) occurring in a trad. of Umm-Khálid; but it is differently related; some saying sanaho sanaho ; and some, sanaAn ; and pronouncing each with, as well as without, teshdeed: so in the Nh. (TA.)

definition: , applied to a portion of time, (M,) signifying A year, syn.
sourceDefinition: , applied to a portion of time, (M,) signifying A year, syn. HawolN , (Mgh,) or EaAmN , (K,) but a distinction is made between EaAmN and sanapN , [as has been stated in art. snh ,] (TA,) belongs to arts. snw and snh [in both of which it is mentioned in many of the lexicons: see what has been said respecting it in art. snh in the present work]: (M:) accord. to Suh, in the R, it is from sanaA , aor. yasonuw , said of a beast [turning a water-wheel], meaning “ he turned round about the well; ” so that it signifies a single revolution of the sun; and it is sometimes termed daArN : he says also that it is longer than the EaAm , which is applied to the [twelve] Arabian months [collectively]: but sanapN is also applied to twelve revolutions of the moon: the sanap $amosiy~ap [or solar year ] is three hundred and sixty-five days and a quarter of a day: and the sanap qamariy~ap [or lunar year ] is three hundred and fifty-four days and a third of a day: it is also said, on the authority of Er-Rághib, that sanapN is used as denoting a year in which is difficulty, and drought, or barrenness, or dearth; and EaAmN , as denoting that in which is ampleness of the means, or circumstances, of life, and abundance of herbage or the like; and by this is explained the nice point in the words of the Kur [xxix. 13], A^alofa sanapK A_il~aA xamosiyna EaAmFA [ a thousand years save fifty years ]; because the fifty years passed before the mission of the prophet [Noah], before which no harm happened to him from his people; but after his mission, the years were difficult to him. (TA.) [Respecting the dims., (which are sun~y~apN and sunayohapN , the former accord. to those who make the original of sanapN to be sanowapN , and the latter accord. to those who make it to be sanohapN ,) and the pls., (which are sanawaAtN and sanahaAtN and sinuwna and sunuwna and siniynN and siniyna , the last whereof is originally siniynN , and suniY~N also,) see sanapN in art. snh ― -b2- Also respecting sanapN used alone as signifying (tropical:) Drought, or barrenness, or vehement or intense drought, see that word in art. snh . -A2- Also respecting the same word used as an epithet, applied to land ( A^aroDN ), as meaning (tropical:) Affected with drought or barrenness, like sanowaA='u and sanohaA='u , see that same word in art. snh .]

definition: A certain well-known bird, (K, TA,) of those that prey;
sourceDefinition: A certain well-known bird, (K, TA,) of those that prey; (Msb, * TA;) it is of the birds called Suquwr [pl. of SaqorN ], as are also the baA$aq and the baAziY and the zur~aq and the yuw^oyuw^ ; (AHát in “ the Book of Birds, ” TA in art. b$q ;) [said by Golius, on the authority of Dmr, to be the white falcon; and to this bird it is perhaps applied by some of the Arabs; but some of them, I believe most of them, and I believe also that they do so most properly, apply this appellation in the present day to the gerfalcon, which is not wholly white; and some, to the falcon gentle: ] the word is [of Pers. origin,] not genuine Arabio; (TA;) it is an arabicized word: the pl. is $awaAhiynu , and sometimes $ayaAhiynu is used in its stead, formed by substituion [of Y for w ] for facilitating the pronunciation. (Msb.) ― -b2- Also (assumed tropical:) The Eamuwd [meaning beam ] of the balance. (K.) ― -b3- And i. q. SanojapN [which signifies A balance, and a steelyard, and a weight of a balance ]: so in the Expos. of the “ Muwatta. ” (MF, TA.)

(L, TA.)

Winter ]; (S;) one of the quarters [ of the circle ] of the seasons; (K;) and ↓ $aAtaApN signifies the same; (Sgh, K;) [and so does ↓ $atiy~apN ; (see an ex. voce riboEiY~N ;)] and so does ↓ ma$otaApN : (Msb, TA:) [also the half-year commencing at the autumnal equinox: ] ISk says, Als~anapu is with the Arabs a name for twelve months: then they divided it into two halves, and commenced the sanap [or year] at the commencement of the $itaA=' because this word is masc. and the word Sayof [meaning in this case the “ half-year commencing at the vernal equinox ”] is fem.: then they divided the $itaA=' into two halves; the $twY being the former; and the rbyE , the latter; [but this is a manifest mistake, probably attributable to a copyist; for, as is well known, the former half is called the rabiyE ; and the latter, the $itaA=' or ↓ $atowap ;] each consisting of three months; and in like manner the Sayof and the qayoZ consist, each, of three months: (TA:) also one of the six seasons into which the year is divided, each whereof consists of two months; namely, the season [ commencing in November and ending in January, ] next after that called Alxariyfu : (S and K voce rabiyEN : [see this word; and see, again, the former of the two tables mentioned above:]) accord. to Mbr, (S,) $itaA='N is pl. of ↓ $atowapN ; (S, Msb, K;) it is said to be so by IF on the authority of Kh, and by some on the authority of Fr or some other: or $itaA='N and ↓ $atowapN signify the same, (K,) as is said in the M; (TA;) [i. e.] some say that Al$~itaA='u is a proper name for the quarter [&c.]: (Msb:) the pl. is A^a$otiyapN , (S, Msb, K,) i. e. pl. of $itaA='N , (S, Msb,) because A^afoEilapN , as pl. of fiEaAlN , is peculiar to a masc. [noun]; (Msb;) and $utiY~N also, (K, TA,) originally A^u$otuwYN [a mistake for $utuwYN ], written in the Tekmileh $itiY~N , as on the authority of Fr.: (TA:) the pl. of its syn. ↓ ma$otaApN is ma$aAtK . (Msb.) ― -b2- Also, i. e. $itaA='N , Hail, syn. baradN , (K, TA, [in the CK barodN ,]) that falls from the sky. (TA.) ― -b3- And Drought, or dearth: (K, and Ham pp. 117 and 150:) this meaning being assigned to the $tA=' exclusively of the Sayof because in it the people keep to the tents, not going forth to seek after herbage. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (L, K,) sec. pers. $arirota , (S, Msb, K, MF,) aor. ya$ar~u ; (L, Msb, MF;) and sec. pers. $arurota , (S accord. to some copies, L, Msb, K, MF,) aor. ya$ur~u ; (L, Msb, K, * MF;) and sec. pers. $ararota , (S accord. to some copies, M, K, MF,) aor. ya$ir~u ; (M, K, MF;) of which three vars. the first is the best known; and the last is strange, and disallowed by most authorities; (MF;) inf. n. [of the first or third] $ar~N (S, K) and [of the first] $ararN (S) and [of the second or third] $araArapN , (S, K,) and $ir~apN also is an inf. n. [syn. with $ar~N ]; (S;) He (a man) was, or became, evil, a wrongdoer, unjust, bad, corrupt, wicked, mischievous, vitious, or depraved. (S, * L, Msb, K, * &c.) The manner in which the K mentions $ar~a with the two aors. ya$ur~u and ya$ir~u [only, omitting the most common aor., i. e. ya$ar~u ,] obviously demands consideration. (MF.) One says, $arirota yaA rajulu [ Thou hast been evil, or a wrongdoer, &c., O man ], (S, K,) and so $arurota and $ararota . (S accord. to different copies, and K.) ― -b2- $ar~a , aor. ya$ar~u , also signifies He increased in evil, wrongdoing, &c. (L.) It is said in a prov., kul~amaA takobaru ta$ar~u [ In proportion as thou growest old, thou increasest in evil, &c.]. (AZ, L.) ― -b3- maA $ar~ahu : see 4, last sentence. -A2- $ar~ahu , (O, K,) aor. ya$ur~u , (O, TA,) inf. n. $ur~N , (O, K,) with damm, (K, [which is said in the TA to indicate that the aor., not the inf. n., is with damm, but this is inconsistent with the common practice of the author of the K, and is evidently wrong,]) He blamed him; found fault with him; attributed or imputed to him, charged him with, or accused him of, a vice, fault, defect, blemish, or something amiss. (O, K, * TA. [See also 4.]) One says, maA qulotu *aAka li$ur~ika waA_in~amaA qulotupu ligayori $ur~ika I said not that to find fault with thee, but I only said it for a different purpose than that of finding fault with thee: (S, TA:) or this has a different meaning, which see below, voce $ur~N . (TA.) One says also, qado qabilotu EaTiy~ataka vum~a radadotuhaA Ealayoka mino gayori $ur~ika walaA Dur~ika , meaning [ I have accepted thy gift; then I have given it back to thee ] without rejecting it to thee or blaming thee [ and without injuring thee ]. (IAar, TA.) -A3- Also $ar~ahu , (S,) or $ar~ahu fiY Al$~amosi , (A,) [aor. and inf. n. as in the next sentence;] and ↓ $r~rhu , (A,) inf. n. ta$oriyrN ; (S;) and ↓ A$r~hu ; and ↓ $aro$arahu ; (A;) He spread it (i. e. a garment, or piece of cloth, S, or some other thing, TA) in the sun: (S, A, TA:) this is the primary signification. (TA.) And [hence,] $ar~ahu , (S, K,) aor. ya$ur~u . (S,) inf. n. $ar~N ; (S, K;) and ↓ A$r~hu , (K,) inf. n. A_i$oraArN ; (TA;) and ↓ $r~rhu , (K,) inf. n. as above; (TA;) and $ar~aAhu [or $araAhu without tesh-deed?]; (K;) He put it (i. e. [the preparation of curd called] A^aqoT , and flesh-meat, S, K, and the like, and salt, S, and a garment, or piece of cloth, and the like, K) upon a xaSafap , (S, K,) i. e. a mat, (TA,) or some other thing, (K,) to dry. (S, K.) And $r~hu He sprinkled it; namely, salt. (R, MF.)

definition: (S, A, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: (S, A, Msb, K, &c.) and ↓ $ur~N , (Kr, K,) the former of which is the more chaste, (TA,) and ↓ $ir~apN (Ham p. 629) Evil, [ moral and physical; ] (L, Msb;) wrongdoing, injustice, badness, corruptness, wickedness, mischievousness, vitiousness, or depravity: (Msb:) [and evil fortune, misfortune, woe, or unhappiness: ] contr. of xayorN : (S, A, K:) pl. $uruwrN . (Msb, K.) It is said in a trad., in a form of prayer, (TA,) used by the Prophet, (Msb,) waAlxayoru kul~uhu biyadayoka waAl$~ar~u layosa A_ilayoka , (Msb, * TA,) meaning [ And all good is in thy hands, and evil i. e.] wrongdoing, or injustice, or corruptness, is not imputable to Thee: (Msb, TA:) or evil is not a means of advancement in thy favour, or of obtaining thine approval: or evil speech does not ascend to Thee. (Nh, L.) ― -b2- $ar~N also signifies (assumed tropical:) Poverty. (K.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) Fever. (K.) ― -b4- It is also an epithet, applied to a man, (Yoo, S,) and so is ↓ $ariyrN , (Akh, S, A, Msb, K,) meaning Evil, wrongdoing, unjust, bad, corrupt, wicked, mischievous, vitious, or depraved: (Yoo, * Akh, * S, * A, * Msb, K: *) [fem. of the former $ar~apN , like as xayorapN is fem. of its contr. xayorN ; and $ur~aY , fem. of A^a$ar~u , is used in the same sense, as will be shown in what follows:] the pl. of $ar~N , (Yoo, S,) or of ↓ $ariyrN , (Akh, S, Msb, K,) is A^a$oraArN , (Yoo, Akh, S, Msb, K,) and of the former $iraArN ; (Ham p. 514;) and you say qawomN A^a$ir~aA='u [pl. of $ar~N or of ↓ $ariyrN ]. (S.) A woman of the Arabs, (S, L,) who, accord. to some, was of the Benoo-'Ámir, (L,) is related to have said, ↓ A^uEiy*uki biA@ll~`hi mino nafosK Har~aY waEayonK $ur~aY , meaning [ I charm thee by invoking God, against a thirsty soul, and ] an evil, or a malignant, eye: (S, L:) or an eye that looks at one with vehement hatred. (TA.) And Al$~ar~u [ The evil one ] is an appellation of Iblees. (K.) ― -b5- [It is also used to denote the comparative and superlative degrees; like the contr. xayorN .] You say, huwa $ar~N minoka [ He is worse, or more evil or wrongdoing &c., than thou ]. (K.) And h`*aA $ar~N mino *aAka [ This is worse, &c., than that ]. (Msb.) And fulaAnN $ar~u Aln~aAsi [ Such a one is the worst, &c., of mankind ]; (S;) and ↓ A^a$ar~u ; (S, Msb, K;) this latter being the original, (Mgh, Msb,) but rare, (K,) or bad, (S, K,) peculiar to the dial. of the Benoo-'Ámir, (Msb,) or unused. (Mgh.) The fem. [of $ar~N ] is $ar~apN , [like as the fem. of its contr., xayorN , is xayorapN ,] (K,) and (of A^a$ar~u , S, * or of $ar~N , which is used for A^a$ar~u , Kr) ↓ $ur~aY . (S, Kr, K.) And [using the dim. form of $ar~N ,] you say, minoka ↓ huwa $urayorN [ He is a little worse, &c., than thou ]. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA in art. xyr . [See xayorN .]) -A2- maA $ar~a for maA A^a$ar~a : see 4.

(TA.) -A2- $iwaA='N $aro$arN Roasted flesh-meat, of which the grease, or gravy, drips; (S, K;) like $alo$alN and ra$oraA$N . (TA.)

definition: , ('Ináyeh, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ $uro$urapN , (so in other copies of the K, accord.
sourceDefinition: , ('Ináyeh, and so in some copies of the K,) or ↓ $uro$urapN , (so in other copies of the K, accord. to the TA,) sing. of $araA$iru , (K,) which signifies The fringe-like extremities of a tail; (S, * K, * A, TA;) and of wings. (TA.) ― -b2- Hence, metaphorically, [or synecdochically,] the pl. is used as signifying (tropical:) The whole: and hence the saying, A^aloqaY Ealayohi $araA$irahu (tropical:) He betook himself altogether to it; as though, says As, by reason of his eagerness, he threw himself altogether upon it: accord. to EshShiháb, it means he betook himself [ to it ], openly or secretly: or $araA$iru signifies (assumed tropical:) the whole body; (K;) and AlqY Elyh $rA$rh and A^ajoraAnahu and A^ajoraAmahu , provs. mentioned by Meyd, all signify the same [app. (assumed tropical:) he threw upon it the weight of his body: see Freytag's Arab. Prov., ii. 409 and 410: and see art. jrm ]: or the first of these means (assumed tropical:) he loved it so that he courted death, or destruction, ( Aisotaholaka ,) in his love of it: (TA:) or he loved it with a love that he would not give up, because of his necessity: (Lth, TA:) or (tropical:) he desired it inordinately, or eagerly, and loved it. (A.) [See also A^aloqaY Ealayohi A^arowaAqahu , voce rawoqN . Accord. to different authorities,] $araA$iru also signifies (assumed tropical:) Burdens, or weights; (S, K;) sing. $aro$arapN : (S:) and it is so expl. as used in the saying mentioned above: or it there signifies (assumed tropical:) weight, and whole person: or the reduplication implies intensiveness; as though this word originally signified weight of evil: but F, in his comments on the Preface of the Ksh, objects to this, as the word does not imply the contr. of xayorN , but dispersion. (TA.) Also (tropical:) Self: (K, TA:) and the saying mentioned above is expl. as meaning (tropical:) He threw himself upon it, through inordinate, or eager, desire, and love. (S, TA.) And (assumed tropical:) Love: (K:) or (assumed tropical:) love of self. (Kr, TA.)

definition: A certain bird, (K, TA,) of small size;
sourceDefinition: A certain bird, (K, TA,) of small size; said by As to be thus called by the people of El- Hijáz; and by the Arabs of the desert, baroqa$ [a mistranscription for biroqi$ ]: it is said to be dustcoloured; in elegance, like the Hum~arap ; and to be a little larger than the EuSofuwr [or sparrow ]. (L, TA.) [Freytag, on the authority of Dmr, says that it is the same as is called Abw brAq$ : (but see biroqi$N :) and describes it as being of an ashy colour, with some mixture of redness; and of the passerine kind. ]

definition: A xaSafap , (S, K,) i.

(K, TA.) -A2- Also A great herd of camels: (K:) because scattered. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. $ufuwfN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and $afiyfN (S, O, K) and $afafN , (CK, [but not in my MS. copy of the K nor in the TA,]) It (a garment, or piece of cloth,) was thin, fine, or delicate, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) so that what was behind it was visible, (S, * IB, Mgh, [for xalaqahu in some copies of the S, and xalofahu in others, I read maA xalofahu , which is the right reading accord. to IB and the TA, agreeably with the reading in the Mgh, which is maA waraA='ahu ,]) or so as to tell what was beneath it: (O, K:) [and it, (a gem, or the like,) was translucent: or was transparent. (See $af~aAfN .)] One says, $af~a Ealayohi vawobuhu His garment was thin, &c., upon him. (S.) ― -b2- ― -b3- And $af~a jisomuhu , aor. , inf. n. $ufuwfN , His body became lean, or emaciated. (S, O, K.) -A2- $af~a , aor. , inf. n. $if~N , It (a thing, O, Msb) exceeded; or was, or became, redundant. (S, O, Msb, K.) Hence, in a trad., $af~a naHowFA mino daAniqK It exceeded by about a dAnq . (Sh, O.) And one says, $af~a Ealayoh , aor. ya$uf~u , [so in the L and TA, contr. to rule, probably a mistranscription for ya$if~u ,] inf. n. $ufuwfN ; and ↓ $f~f , and ↓ Ast$f~ ; [app. meaning, as seems to be indicated by the context, It exceeded it: ] and $afifotu fiY Als~iloEapi [app. a mistranscription for $afafotu ] I gained in, or upon, the the article of merchandise: (TA: [and so, app., ↓ $af~afotu : see $af~aY :]) and fY tijaAratihi ↓ Ast$f~ [ He obtained what is termed $if~N in his traffic; i. e.] he made gain, or profit, in his traffic; syn. rabiHa . (S and K in art. rbH .) ― -b2- And sometimes (Msb) it signifies also the contr.; i. e. It fell short; or was, or became, deficient. (Msb, K.) One says, (O, Msb,) of a dirhem, (O,) h`*aA ya$if~u qaliylFA This falls short, or is deficient, a little. (O, Msb.) And $af~a Eanohu Alv~awobu , aor. , The garment was too short for him. (TA.) -A3- Also $af~a , (O, K,) aor. , (O,) It (a thing, O) was, or became, in a state of motion, commotion, or agitation. (O, K.) -A4- And $af~a laka Al$~aYo'u i. q. daAma and vabata [app. meaning The thing belonged, or pertained, to thee permanently, or constantly; or may the thing belong, &c.]. (TA.) -A5- $af~ahu , (S, M, O, K,) aor. , inf. n. $af~N (S, M, TA) and $ufuwfN , (M, TA,) It (anxiety) rendered him lean, or emaciated; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ $afo$afahu ; (S;) both are also expl. as meaning it rendered him lean, or lank in the belly, so that he became slender: (TA:) or, accord. to the M, it (grief, and love,) pained his heart: or rendered him lean, or emaciated: or deprived him of his reason: and it is said of grief as meaning it manifested what he felt of impatience. (TA.) And $af~a Aln~ufuwsa , as used in a verse of Towbeh Ibn-El- Homeiyir, It hurt and melted the souls. (Ham p. 594.) -A6- See also 8, in two places.

definition: (S, O, K) kul~ahu (K) He drank what was in the vessel, all of it, (S, O, K,) even the $ufaAfap [or last drop or remains ], (O,) not leaving any of it remaining;
sourceDefinition: (S, O, K) kul~ahu (K) He drank what was in the vessel, all of it, (S, O, K,) even the $ufaAfap [or last drop or remains ], (O,) not leaving any of it remaining; (S;) [and so Aijotaf~a ;] as also ↓ t$Af~ : (S, O, K:) and ↓ Ast$f~ AlmaA='a He drank the water to the uttermost, not leaving any of it remaining; as also ↓ $af~ahu , aor. , inf. n. $af~N : and AlmaA='a ↓ $afafotu I drank much of the water without having my thirst satisfied. (TA.) [Hence,] in the trad. of Umm-Zara, waA_ino $ariba A@$otaf~a [ And if he drank, he drank up all that was in the vessel ]. (S, O.) And it is said in a prov., ↓ layosa Alr~iY~u Eani Alt~a$aAf~i (S, O, TA) i. e. The satisfying of thirst is not from the drinking up all that is in the vessel; for it is sometimes effected by less than this: (O, TA:) it is applied in forbidding one's going to the utmost in an affair, and persevering therein. definition: A thin, fine, or delicate, garment or piece of cloth;
sourceDefinition: A thin, fine, or delicate, garment or piece of cloth; (AZ, S, Mgh, O, * Msb, K; *) as also ↓ $if~N (AZ, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ $afiyfN : (Msb:) you say vawobN $af~N (S, Mgh, Msb) and ↓ $if~N (S, Msb) and ↓ $afiyfN . (Msb:) [see also $af~aAfN :] and the garment, or piece of cloth, itself, is termed $af~N and ↓ $if~N : (Har p. 70:) [i. e. each of these words is also used as a subst.; and this is perhaps meant in the O and K: or] $af~N signifies also a certain thin, fine, or delicate, veil or covering: or, accord. to Aboo-Nasr, a certain thin, fine, or delicate, veil or covering, of wool, through which one sees what is behind it: (S:) pl. $ufuwfN . (O, Msb, K.) Among the verses of “ the Book ” [of Sb, cited as exs. therein], is the following: lalobosu EabaA='apK wataqar~u EayoniY A^aHab~u A_ilaY~a mino lubosi Al$~ufuwfi [ Verily the wearing of a woollen cloak, my eye being therewithal unheated by tears, is more pleasing to me than the wearing of thin, fine, or delicate, garments ]. (O.) -A2- See also $if~N . -A3- $f~ [app. $af~N ] also signifies Pimples, or small pustules, that come forth and then go away. (Ibn-Buzurj, TA.)

definition: He wrapped, or inwrapped, himself with his garment;
sourceDefinition: He wrapped, or inwrapped, himself with his garment; syn. talaf~afa : (S, O:) or A$tml biAlv~awobi signifies he wrapped the garment around the whole of his body so that his arm, or hand, did not come forth from it: (K:) or, as some say, he wrapped himself with the garment, and threw [ a part of ] it upon his left side. (TA.) [See also 5.] Ai$otimaAlu AlS~am~aA='i , which is forbidden by the Prophet, is, accord. to As, The wrapping oneself with the garment so as to cover with it his body, not raising a side thereof in such a manner that there is in it an opening from which he may put forth his hand, or arm: (O:) this is also termed Alt~alaf~uEu : and sometimes one reclines in the state thus described: (TA:) but A 'Obeyd says, accord. to the explanation of the lawyers, it is the wrapping oneself with one garment, not having upon him another, then raising it on one side and putting it upon his shoulders: [so says Sgh; and he adds,] he who explains it thus has regard to the dislike of one's uncovering himself and exposing to view the pudenda; and he who explains it as do the lexicologists dislikes one's covering his whole body for fear of his becoming in a state in which his respiration would become obstructed so that he would perish: (O:) or it is one's covering his whole body with the kisaA=' or with the A_izaAr ; (S, Msb;) to which some add, not raising aught of the sides thereof. (Msb.) [See also art. Sm .] One says also, ya$otamilu EalaY Als~ayfi [ He wraps his garment over the sword; or] he covers the sword with his garment. (S, O.) ― -b2- [Hence, A$tml EalaY ka*aA It comprehended, or comprised, such a thing. ] One says, Alr~aHimu ta$otamilu EalaY Alwaladi (assumed tropical:) The womb comprises [or encloses ] the young. (TA.) [And in like manner one says of a woman, A$tmlt minohu EalaY waladK (assumed tropical:) She became with child by him. And AlkitaAbu ya$otamilu EalaY ka*aA waka*aA (assumed tropical:) The book, or writing, comprises such and such things. And hence the phrase in grammar, badalu A@$otimaAlK (assumed tropical:) A substitute for an antecedent to indicate an implication therein.] ― -b3- One says also, A$tml Ealayohi AlA^amoru , meaning (tropical:) The event [such as a misfortune or an evil of any kind beset him, or beset him on every side, or] encompassed him; (K, TA;) like as the kisaA=' encompasses the body. (TA.) ― -b4- One says of wine, ta$otamilu EalaY AlEaqoli fatamolikuhu wata*ohabu bihi (assumed tropical:) [ It compasses the intellect, and so takes possession of it, and makes away with it ]: (Ham p. 555:) or ta$otamilu EalaY Eaqoli AlA_inosaAni fatugay~ibuhu (assumed tropical:) [ It compasses the intellect of the man, and conceals it ]; and thus one says of the present world or its enjoyments ( Ald~unoyaA ). (TA.) [ A$tml EalaY $aYo'K often means (assumed tropical:) He took, or got, possession of a thing; got it, or held it, within his grasp, or in his possession. ] ― -b5- [Hence,] one says, A$tml EalaY naAqapK fa*ahaba bihaA (assumed tropical:) He mounted a she-camel and went away with her. (AZ, O.) ― -b6- And A$tml Ealayohi (assumed tropical:) He shrouded, covered, or protected, him with himself, or his own person. (TA.) ― -b7- See also 7

definition: A state of union or composedness: and a state of disunion or discomposedness: thus having two contr.
sourceDefinition: A state of union or composedness: and a state of disunion or discomposedness: thus having two contr. significations: (MF, TA:) or a united, or composed, state of the affairs, (S, Msb, TA,) and of the number, (TA,) of a people, or company of men: (S, Msb, TA:) and a disunited, or discomposed, state of the affairs [&c.] thereof. (S, Mgh, Msb.) In imprecating evil upon enemies, (O, TA,) [or upon an enemy,] one says, $at~ata A@ll~`hu $amolahumo , (O, TA,) or far~aqa A@ll~`hu $amolahumo , (Msb,) or fr~q All~`h $amolahu , (S,) i. e. [ May God dissolve, break up, discompose, derange, disorganize, disorder, or unsettle, ] their, (Msb,) or his, (S,) united, or composed, state of affairs; (S, Msb;) and $at~a $amoluhumo i. e. [ May their united, or composed, state of affairs &c.] become dissolved, broken up, discomposed, &c.: (O, TA:) and [in the contr. case] one says, jamaEa A@ll~`hu $amolahumo , (S, O, Msb, TA,) or $amolahu , (Mgh,) i. e. [ May God unite, or compose, ] their, (S, Msb,) or his, (Mgh,) disunited, or discomposed, state of affairs [&c.]. (S, Mgh, Msb.) And ↓ $amalN signifies the same: El-Ba'eeth says, qado yanoEa$u A@ll~`hu AlfataY baEoda EavorapK waqado yajomaEu A@ll~`hu Al$~atiyta mina Al$~amalo [ Sometimes, or often, God raises the young man after a stumble: and sometimes, or often, God unites, or composes, what is dissolved, or broken up, of the state of affairs previously united, or composed ]: (S, O:) AZ cites this ex. in his “ Nawádir: ” (S:) but Aboo-'Omar El-Jarmee says that he had not heard the word thus except in this verse: (S, O:) Ibn-Buzurj, however, cites another verse as presenting an ex. of the same. (TA.) ― -b2- daxala fiY $amolihaA and ↓ $amalihaA , said of a he-camel that has become concealed among a herd of [she-] camels, means He entered amid their dense multitude: (K, TA:) so in the M and the Moheet. (TA.) -A2- Also, (AHn, O, K,) and so ↓ $imolN , and ↓ $imil~N , (K,) A raceme of a palm-tree: (AHn, O, K:) Et-Tirimmáh likens thereto a camel's tail: (TA:) or such as has little fruit: (K:) or of which some of the fruit has been plucked: but AO used to say that it is the produce [or spadix ] of the male palm-tree, while not abundant and large. (TA.) -A3- See also $amaAlN . -A4- And $amolN mino junuwnK signifies Fear, or fright, like insanity: and so ↓ $amalN [used alone, and thus written]. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A [ garment of the kind called ] kisaA=' , with which one wraps, or inwraps, himself ( yu$otamalu bihi ), (S, Mgh, K,) smaller than the qaTiyfap ; as also ↓ mi$omalN (K) and ↓ mi$omalapN ; (S, K;) the last two expl. by Lth as a kisaA=' having a sparse villous substance, with which one wraps himself, smaller than the qaTiyfap : (TA:) or the first signifies a small kisaA=' which one wears in the manner of the A_izaAr [or waist-wrapper ]: (Msb:) or with the Arabs it is a miy^ozar [or waist-wrapper ] of wool or of [ goats' ] hair, which one wraps round him: and ↓ mi$omalapN , such as is made of two pieces sewed together, with which a man wraps himself when he sleeps by night: (Az, TA:) and this last, accord. to Meyd, signifies a kisaA=' comprising the steel with which one strikes fire, with the apparatus of this latter: (Har p. 628:) the pl. of the first is $imaAlN (Msb, TA) and $amalaAtN . (Msb.) [See also mi$omaAlN .] ― -b2- [Hence the saying,] Dam~a Ealayohi All~ayolu $amolatahu (tropical:) [ The night contracted upon him its covering of darkness ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And A^um~u $amolapa (tropical:) The present world, or its enjoyments; syn. definition: , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K, &c.,) applied to one of the hands or arms, (S, Msb,) The left; contr. of yamiynN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) as also ↓ $iymaAlN , (K, TA, [in the CK, Al$~amAl and Al$~mAl are erroneously put for Al$~imaAl and Al$~iymaAl ,]) the latter thought by ISd to be used only by poetic license, for $imaAlN , (TA,) and ↓ $imolaAlN , (AA, S, O, K,) this last not known to Ks nor to As: (TA:) of the fem. gender: (S, O, Msb:) pl. [of pauc.] A^a$omulN , (S, O, Msb, K,) because it is fem., (S, O,) and [of mult.] $amaAy^ilu , (S, O, Msb, K,) which is anomalous, (S, O,) and $umulN , and $imaAlN like the sing. (K.) ― -b2- And The direction [or side ] of the hand so called: you say, Ailotafata yamiynFA wa$imaAlFA i. e. [ He looked, or turned his face, ] in the direction of the ymyn and in the direction of the $mAl : and the pl. in this sense also is A^u$omulN and $amaAy^ilu : (Msb:) you say, *ahaba A_ilaY A^ayomuni AlA_ibili waA^a$omulihaA He went to the right sides of the camels and the left sides thereof. (TA in art. ymn .) ― -b3- [Hence,] (tropical:) Ill luck, unluckiness, or evil fortune. (K, TA.) Tayoru Al$~imaAli means (tropical:) Birds of ill luck: (A, TA:) every bird from which one augurs evil. (O, TA.) One says, jaraY lahu guraAbu $imaAlK , meaning (assumed tropical:) What was disliked, or hated, happened to him: as though the bird [to which this is likened] came to him from the $imaAl [or direction of the left hand]. (TA.) And when the place that a person occupies is rendered evil, one says, fulaAnN EinodiY biAl$~imaAli (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one is with me, or in my estimation, in an evil plight ]. (TA.) ― -b4- See also $amaAlN . ― -b5- Also Every handful of corn, or seedproduce, which the reaper grasps [app. because grasped with his left hand]. (K.) -A2- And A sort of bag that is put upon the udder of the ewe or goat (S, O, K) when it (i. e. the udder, TA) is heavy [ with milk ]: (K, * TA:) or it is peculiar to the she-goat: (K:) pl. $umulN . (K voce EaraAbapN .) ― -b2- And A similar thing that is put to the raceme of a palm-tree, made with pieces of [ the garments called ] A^akosiyap [pl. of kisaA='N ], in order that the fruit may not be shaken off. (S, O.) [In this sense it may perhaps be from the same word as pl. of $amolapN .] -A3- And A mark made with a hot iron ( simapN ) upon the udder of a ewe or goat. (K.) -A4- Also A nature; or a natural disposition or temper or the like: (O, Msb, K:) accord. to Er-Rághib, so called because [it is as though it were a thing] inwrapping the man [and restricting his freedom of action], like as the [garments called] $imaAl [pl. of $amolapN ] inwrap the body: (TA:) the pl. is $amaAy^ilu , (O, K, TA,) and $imaAlN , also, [which seems to be rarely used as a sing. in this sense,] may be a pl., like dilaASN . (TA; and Ham p. 489, q. v.) 'Abd-Yaghooth El-Hárithee says, A^alamo taEolamaA A^an~a AlmalaAmapa nafoEuhaA qaliylN wamaA lawomiY A^axiYmino $imaAliyaA [ Know not ye two that the utility of censure is little, and my censuring my brother is not of my nature, or of my natural dispositions? ]: (O, TA:) here it may be a pl., of the class of hijaAnN and dilaASN : or it may be [ $amaAliyaA ,] an instance of transposition, for $amaAy^iliY . (TA.) -A5- See also $imil~N .

definition: A man smitten, or blown upon, by the [ north, or northerly, ] wind called $amaAl : (S, O:) and in like manner, a meadow, and a pool of water left by a torrent;
sourceDefinition: A man smitten, or blown upon, by the [ north, or northerly, ] wind called $amaAl : (S, O:) and in like manner, a meadow, and a pool of water left by a torrent; (O;) or, applied to this last, smitten by the wind thus called so as to become cool: (S:) and hence, with p , wine (tropical:) cool to the taste; (S, O, TA; *) or wine exposed to the $amaAl and so rendered cool and pleasant: (TA: see also $amuwlN :) and fire upon which the wind called the $amaAl has blown: (S, O:) and a night cold, with [ wind that is called ] $amaAl . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (tropical:) One whose natural dispositions are liked, approved, or found pleasant: (K:) from [the same epithet applied to] water upon which the $amaAl has blown, and which it has cooled: or, as ISd thinks, from $amuwlN [q. v.]: (TA:) or ma$omuwlu AlxalaAy^iqi a man whose natural dispositions are commended; as being likened to wine that is commended: and also whose natural dispositions are discommended; as though from Al$~amaAlu , because they do not commend it when it disperses the clouds: (Har p. 285:) [for] A^axolaAqN ma$omuwlapN [sometimes] means discommended, evil, natural dispositions. (IAar, ISk, TA.) The saying of Aboo-Wejzeh, ma$omuwlapu AlA^unosi majonuwbN mawaAEiduhaA is expl. by IAar as meaning (assumed tropical:) Her familiarity passes away with the $amaAl , and her promises pass away with the januwb [which is the opposite of the $amaAl ]: or, as some relate it, majonuwbapu AlA^unosi ma$omuwlN mawaAEiduhaA [meaning in like manner, as is said in the TA, on the authority of IAar, in art. jnb : or,] accord. to ISk, meaning her familiarity is commended, because the jnwb , with rain, is desired for abundance of herbage; and her promises are not commended. (TA.) ― -b3- nawFY ma$omuwlapN , a phrase used by Zuheyr, is expl. as meaning (assumed tropical:) [ A tract, or place, towards which one journeys, ] that separates friends; because the [wind called] $amaAl disperses the clouds: (TA:) or it means quickly [or soon ] becoming exposed to view; (ISk, O, TA;) from the fact that when the wind called the $amaAl blows the clouds, they delay not to become cleared away, and to depart: (O:) or, accord. to IAar, it means maA^oxuw*N bihaA *aAtu Al$~imaAli [ in which the direction of the left hand is taken ]. (TA.) ― -b4- In the saying, Hamalato bihi fiY layolapK ma$omuwlapN the meaning is, fariEapN [i. e. One in a state of fright became pregnant with him in a certain night ]. (TA, referring to the phrase $amolN mino junuwnK .)

(TA.) ― -b3- See also 4, last sentence but one. -A2- SaHaba , aor. , (K,) inf. n. SaHobN , (TK,) He skinned a slaughtered animal. (K.)

definition: [ I made such a one to be a companion, or an associate, to him ].
sourceDefinition: [ I made such a one to be a companion, or an associate, to him ]. (A.) And A^aSoHabotuhu Al$~aYo'a (tropical:) I made the thing to be [ as it were ] a companion to him; (S, K, TA;) and so ↓ AstSHbthu ; as in the saying, AstSHbth AlkitaAba wagayorahu (tropical:) I made the book, or writing, &c., to be [ as it were ] his companion. (S, * TA.) ― -b2- And ASHbhu (tropical:) He did to him that which caused him to be a companion, or an associate, to him. (A, TA.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) He left upon it, namely, a skin, its hair, (S, A,) or its wool; not subjecting it to the process termed EaTonN . (S.) ― -b4- See also 1, in three places. -A2- ASHb , intrans., He (a man) became one having a companion, or an associate: (K, TA: [in the latter said to be tropical; but, I think, without reason:]) and he was, or became, one having companions, or associates. (TA.) ― -b2- And [hence,] (tropical:) He (a man) had a son who had attained to manhood (S, A, TA) and so become like him: (TA;) i. e. he was alone, and became one having a companion; (A;) or as though his son became his companion. (TA.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) He (a camel, and a horse or similar beast, S, TA, or an animal, and a man to a man, A, TA *) became tractable, submissive, or obsequious, after being refractory, or incompliant; (S, A, TA;) [and so ↓ SaAHaba , as is implied by an explanation of its part. n. muSaAHibN ; and ↓ AstSHb , for] hence, (A,) one says also, AisotaSoEaba tum~a A@sotaSoHaba (tropical:) [ He was refractory, or incompliant: then he became tractable, submissive, or obsequious ]: (A, TA:) and accord. to A 'Obeyd, one says, ↓ SaHibotu Alr~ajula , from AlS~uHobapu , and A^aSoHabotu [app. ASHbt lahu ], meaning (assumed tropical:) I became tractable, submissive, or obsequious, to the man. (TA.) ― -b4- And, said of water, (tropical:) It became overspread with [ the green substance termed ] TuHolub . (S, A. *)

definition: A companion, an associate, a comrade, a fellow, or a friend;
sourceDefinition: A companion, an associate, a comrade, a fellow, or a friend; (A, MA, KL, TA;) a fellow-traveller: (MA:) [ an accomplice: (assumed tropical:) an accompanier, or attendant, as applied to a thing:] and (tropical:) a lord, or master; a possessor, an owner, an occupant, a haver, or a proprietor; of anything: (A, TA:) it is not trans. like the verb, therefore you may not say, zayodN SaAHibN EamorFA ; (TA;) [i. e.] it is not used as an act. part. n., but as a subst., like waAlidN ; (Ham p. 32:) the pl., (S, Msb,) or term applied to a pl. number, (A, K, TA,) is ↓ SaHobN , (S, A, Msb, K,) a pl. like rakobN of raAkibN , (S,) or [rather] a quasi-pl. n., (TA,) and A^aSoHaAbN , [the most common of all,] (A, Msb,) a pl. like A^a$ohaAdN of $aAhidN , (TA,) or pl. of SaHobN , like A^aforaAxN of faroxN , (S,) and A^aSaAHiybu , (S, K,) pl. of A^aSoHaAbN , (S,) and SuHobaAnN , (S, K,) a pl. like $ub~aAnN of $aAb~N , (S,) and SiHaAbN , (S, A, K,) a pl. like jiyaAEN of jaAy^iEN , (S,) and SiHaAbapN , (A, K,) in which the p may be regarded, agreeably with analogy, as an affix to the pl. SiHaAbN characteristic of the fem. gender, (TA,) and ↓ SaHaAbapN , (S, A, Msb, K,) which is more common than SiHaAbapN , (TA,) but the only instance of faEaAlapN as the pl. measure of a word of the measure faAEilN , (L, TA,) or originally an inf. n., (S,) or not so, but a quasi-pl. n., though written like the inf. n. [that is said to be its original], (from a marginal note in a copy of the S,) and ↓ SuHobapN , (S, A,) a pl. like furohapN of faArihN , (S, TA,) or [rather] a quasi-pl. n.: (TA:) the fem. is SaAHibapN , and its pl. is SawaAHibu and SawaAHibaAtN , (Mgh, Msb,) the latter mentioned by AAF on the authority of Abu-l- Hasan: (TA:) hence, in a trad. of 'Áïsheh, A^anotun~a SawaAHibu yuwsufa [ Ye are the female companions, or the mistresses, of Joseph; meaning, enticers to lewdness]; or, as some relate it, SawaAHibaAtu yuwsufa : (Mgh:) the dim. of SaAHibN is ↓ SuwayoHibN (A) [and that of SaAHibahN is ↓ SuwayoHibapN ]. yaASaAHi for yaASaAHibiY [ O my companion, &c.,] is the only allowable instance of such curtailing of a prefixed noun, related as heard from the Arabs. (S, TA.) One says, fulaAnN SaAHibu SidoqK [ Such a one is a good companion, &c.]. (A, * TA.) [And SaAHibu jayo$i The commander of an army. And SaAHibu Albariydi and SaAHibu Al$~uroTapi &c.: see arts. brd and $rT &c. And AlS~aAHibu , alone, in post-classical times applied to The Wezeer, when an officer of the pen: see De Sacy's Chrest. Ar., sec. ed., ii. 59.] And SaAHibu Alyamiyni [ The companion of the right hand ] and SaAHibu Al$~imaAli [ The companion of the left hand ]; appellations of each man's recording angels, who write down his good and evil actions. (A trad. thus commencing in the Jámi' es-Sagheer.) And SaAHibu AlS~uwri (assumed tropical:) The angel who is the possessor of the horn. (Idem.) [And SaAHibu bayotK (assumed tropical:) The owner, or master, of a house or tent. ] And A^aSoHaAbu Aljan~api (assumed tropical:) [ The inmates, or occupants, of Paradise ]: (Kur ii. 76, &c.:) and A^aSoHaAbu Aln~aAri (assumed tropical:) [ The inmates, &c., of the fire of Hell]. (Kur ii. 37, &c.) And SaAHibu sijonK (assumed tropical:) An inmate of a prison. (Bd and Jel in xii. 39.) And SaAHibu AlS~af~i waAljumoEapi (assumed tropical:) He who keeps to praying in the first rank and to the prayer of Friday. (El-Munáwee on a trad. thus commencing in the Jámi' es-Sagheer.) And A^aSojaAbu Al$~aAfiEiY~i (tropical:) The followers of the persuasion of EshSháfi'ee: and in like manner one says of the followers of other persuasions. (Msb.) [And SaAHibu kitaAbK (assumed tropical:) The author of a book. ] And SaAHibu EilomK wamaAlK (tropical:) A possessor of science and of wealth. (A, TA.) And SaAHibu witorK (assumed tropical:) [ One who has a claim for blood-revenge: see an ex. in a verse cited voce dar~aAkN ]. (Keys Ibn-Rifá'ah, TA in art. drk .) [And SaAHibu A^amorK wanahoYK (assumed tropical:) One who possesses authority to command and to forbid. And SaAHibu A^amorK also signifies (assumed tropical:) The author of an affair or event or action; the doer of a thing; the manager, or disposer, thereof: and one who keeps, or adheres, to a thing. And SaAHibu dayonK (assumed tropical:) A debtor. ] And one says, xaraja waSaAHibaAhu Als~ayofu waAlr~umoHu (tropical:) [ He went forth, the sword and the spear being his companions ]. (A, TA.)

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 1. (S, Msb, K.) ― -b2- Also, [as a subst., Epilepsy, or falling sickness: and sometimes, app., ecstatic catalepsy; a sort of trance into which a person falls: ] a certain disease, (S, O, Msb, K,) well known, (S, O,) resembling madness, or diabolical possession, (Msb,) accord. to the Ra-ees [Ibn-Seenà, whom we call “ Avicenna ”], (TA,) preventing, but not completely, the vital organs from performing their actions [or functions ]; the cause of which is an obstruction that occurs in one or more of the venters ( buTuwn ) of the brain and in the ducts of the A^aEoSaAb [here meaning nerves ] by which the members are moved, [ arising ] from an abundant thick or viscous xiloT [or humour ], whereby the ruwH [by which is here meant, as in many other instances, the vital spirit, or nervous fluid, ] is prevented from pervading them in the natural manner, and consequently the members become [ spasmodically ] contracted. (K, TA.) -A2- Also A sort, or species: and a state, condition, or manner of being: syn. DarobN and fan~N : (S, K:) of a thing: (K:) and so ↓ SiroEN : and likewise DaroEN and DiroEN : (TA:) [See also SaroEapN :] pl. [of mult.] SuruwEN (S, K) and [of pauc.] A^aSoruEN . (K.) One says, huwa *uw SaroEayoni , meaning *uw lawonayoni [i. e. He, or it, has two sorts, or species: or two distinctive qualities or properties ]. (Ibn-'Abbád, Z, O, K.) And tarakotuhumo SaroEayoni I left them changing from state to state. (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K.) And liloA^amori SaroEaAni , meaning TarafaAni [i. e. There are two ways of performing the affair, either of which may be chosen ]. (TA.) ― -b2- See also SiroEN , in three places. ― -b3- SaroEaAni Two camels of which one comes to the water when the other returns from it, by reason of their [the camels'] multitude. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- And [hence, perhaps,] AlS~aroEaAni signifies The night and the day; (K;) [and] so ↓ AlS~iroEaAni , with kesr, like AlS~irofaAni : (TA in art. Srf :) or the forenoon and the afternoon; from the first part of day to midday and from midday to sunset; each of these being termed SaroEN : (S, O, K:) or the morning, between daybreak and sunrise, and the evening, between sunset and nightfall; as also AlEaSoraAni ; (S and K in explanation of AlA^aboradaAni ;) and some assert that it is formed by transposition from AlEaSoraAni : (TA:) or the two extremities of the day. (A, TA.) And one says, A^atayotuhu SaroEaYi Aln~ahaAri I came to him in the morning and evening; or between daybreak and sunrise and between sunset and nightfall. (S, O, K.) And laqiytuhu SaroEaYi Aln~ahaAri I met him at the two extremities of the day. (A, TA.) Dhu-r-Rummeh says, kaA^an~aniY naAziEN yavoniyhi Eano waTanK SaroEaAni raAy^iHapF EaqolN wataqoyiydu meaning As though I were one, i. e. a camel, yearning towards his place of abode, which an evening and a morning, in evening a binding of the fore shank to the arm and in the morning a shackling of the legs, turn [or keep ] away from a settled abiding-place: or, as Aboo-'Alee relates it, raAy^iHapN , [as a partial substitute for SaroEaAni ,] meaning, an evening, when there is a binding of the fore shank to the arm, and a morning, when there is a shackling of the legs; for they bind the camel's fore shank to his arm in the evening when he is lying down, and they shackle his legs in the morning so that he may pasture [but not stray]: another reading is SaroEaAhu [ his morning and evening ]. (TA.) ― -b5- One says also, huwa SaroEu ka*aA i. e. Hi*aA='ahu [app. meaning It is over against, or corresponding to, such a thing ]. (O, K.)

definition: A mode, or manner, of throwing down, or prostrating;
sourceDefinition: A mode, or manner, of throwing down, or prostrating; or of being thrown down, or prostrated: (S, * K, TA:) a word similar to rikobapN and jilosapN . (S.) Hence, (K,) one says, suwo'u AlAisotimosaAki xayorN mino Husoni AlS~iroEapi [ The bad manner of holding fast upon one's beast is better than the good manner of being thrown down, or prostrated ]: (S, K:) i. e., when one holds fast, though he ride not well, it is better than one's being thrown down, or prostrated, in a manner that does not hurt him; because he who holds fast sometimes overtakes, but he who is thrown down will not attain: (TA:) a prov.: or, as some relate it, ↓ Husoni AlS~aroEapi , which means the good manner of the single suffering of prostration. (K, * TA. [See also Freytag's Arab. Prov. i. 623.])

definition: One who throws down, or prostrates, others;
sourceDefinition: One who throws down, or prostrates, others; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ Sir~iyEN and ↓ Sur~aAEapN : (K:) or one who throws down, or prostrates, his antagonists much, or often; (TA;) and so ↓ Sir~iyEN , (S, O,) and ↓ Sur~aAEapN , with damm and teshdeed, mentioned by Ks: (O:) or ↓ Sir~iyEN signifies one who throws down, or prostrates, vehemently, though he be not well known for doing so; as also ↓ Sar~aAEN and ↓ SariyEN , the latter like A^amiyrN [in measure, but this I think doubtful, probably added from finding Sir~iyEN mistranscribed]: or ↓ Sir~iyEN , accord. to the T, one whose occupation, whereby he is known, is the throwing down, or prostrating, others [ as a wrestler ]. (TA.) definition: , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (A, Mgh, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_iSolaAHN , (S, A,) and quasi-inf. n. SalaAHN , (L in art. lqH ,) said of a man, (A, Msb,) and of God, (TA,) [and of a thing,] He, and it, made, or rendered, it, or him, good, incorrupt, right, just, righteous, virtuous, or honest; constituted it, disposed it, arranged it, or qualified it, well, rightly, or properly; rectified, corrected, redressed, or reformed, it; put it into a good, incorrupt, sound, right, or proper, state; or restored it to such a state; put it to rights, or in a state of order; set it right, set it in order, ordered it, managed it well, cultured it; adjusted, dressed, or trimmed, it; prepared it properly for use; repaired, mended, amended, or improved, it; made it, or him, to thrive; contr. of A^afosadahu . (S, * K. [And so by implication in the Mgh &c.]) One says, A^aSolaHotu Alqidora biAlt~aAbali [ I made good, qualified properly, or seasoned, ( the contents of ) the cooking-pot with the seeds that are used in cooking ]. (Msb in art. tbl .) And A^aSolaHotu Als~iqaA='a biAlr~ub~i [ I seasoned the skin with rob, or inspissated juice ]. (S in art. rb .) And A^aSolaHotu bayona Alqawomi [in which AlA^amora is understood, so that the meaning is I rectified, or reformed, or amended, the circumstances subsisting between the people, or party; or] I made peace, or I effected a rectification of affairs, an agreement, a harmony, a reconciliation, an accomodation, or an adjustment; [or I adjusted the affair; ] between the people, or party. (Msb.) And saEaY fiY A_iSolAaHi *aAti Albayoni [ He laboured in rectifying, or improving, the bad, or the good, state of circumstances, or the disunion or union, subsisting between people ]. (A.) One says also, ASlH Ald~aAb~apa , (TA,) and ASlH A_ilaY Ald~aAb~api , (T, A, Mgh, TA,) the latter because ASlH implies the meaning of A^aHosana , (Mgh,) (tropical:) He acted well to the beast, (T, A, TA,) and put it into a good, or right, or proper, state, or took care of it, or paid frequent attention to it. (A, TA.) And ASlH A_ilayohi (tropical:) He acted well to him, did good to him, or benefited him. (K, TA.) And ASlH [alone] (assumed tropical:) He did that which was good, right, or just. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , (MA, L, Msb, K,) from SalaHa ; (MA;) and ↓ SaliyHN , (IAar, L, K,) from SaluHa ; (MA;) and ↓ SiloHN ; (K;) applied to a thing, (Msb,) and to a man, (MA,) Good, incorrupt, right, just, righteous, virtuous, or honest; &c.; [see 1; contr. of faAsidN :] (MA, L, K:) pl. SulaHaA='u [accord. to general analogy of SaliyHN , and app. applied only to rational beings, like SaAliHuwna ,] and ↓ SuluwHN [q. v.; this being said by some to be a pl. of SaAliHN ; and by others, to be originally an inf. n.; like as is said of $uhuwdN ]. (L.) One says rajulN SaAliHN fiY nafosihi [ A man good, incorrupt, &c., in himself ], mino qawomK SulaHaA='a [ of a people good, incorrupt, &c.]. (L.) (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SaAliHN signifies also (assumed tropical:) Suitable, fit, or meet: so in the saying, huwa SaAliHN lilowilaAyapi (assumed tropical:) [ He is fit for the office of prefect, or the like ]. (Msb.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) Much, copious, or frequent: one says maTorapN SaAliHapN (tropical:) A copious rain. (Yaakoob, L, TA.) And hence the saying of IJ, A^ubodilati Alt~aA='u mina AlwaAwi A_ibodaAlFA SaAliHFA , meaning (tropical:) [ t is substituted for w ] frequently. (TA.) ― -b4- The A in SaAliHN is [often] omitted in writing [though not in pronunciation] when it is used as a proper name [so that the name is written SlH , or more properly S`liHN ]. (Durrat el-Ghowwás in De Sacy's Anthol. Gram. Ar. p. 66 of the Arabic text.)

definition: A cause, a means, or an occasion, of good;
sourceDefinition: A cause, a means, or an occasion, of good; a thing, an affair, or a business, conducive to good, or that is for good; [and hence it may often be rendered simply an affair, when the context shows it to mean what is conducive to good or done for a good purpose;] contr. of mafosadapN ; (S and Msb and K in art. fsd ;) a good, right, or virtuous, affair; (KL;) a thing that is good and right; syn. ↓ SalaAHN [q. v.]: pl. maSaAliHu . (S, A, Msb, K.) One says, naZara fiY maSAliHi Aln~aAsi [ He considered the things that were for the good of the people ]. (A, TA.) And humo mino A^aholi AlmafaAsidi laA AlmaSaAliHi [ They are of the people who occupy themselves in the things conducive to evil, not the things conducive to good ]. (A, TA. *) And fiY AlA^amori maSolaHapN In the affair is that which is good: (Msb:) [or a cause of good. ] And raA^aY AlA_imaAmu AlmaSolaHapa fiY ka*aA The Imám saw what was good and right [or what was conducive to good ] in such a thing. (TA.) ― -b2- It is also an inf. n. of SalaHa . (MA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, in art. Sbr , M, O, K,) originally ↓ SinaborN , (O,) Cold, as a subst.; (M, O;) as also Sin~iborN : (O:) or cold clouds: (IDrd, O:) or a cold wind (M, K) with mist or clouds: (M:) occurring in a verse of Tarafeh with kesr to the b : (M:) [see also SunobuwrN :] or Sin~abirN , occurring in that verse, signifies the intense cold of winter; (S in art. Sbr ;) as also ↓ SanaAbiru , (S, K,) of which the sing. is ↓ SunobuwrN . (TA.) On the expression of Tarafeh, Hiyna haAja AlS~in~abiro , [ when the cold wind, with mist, rises, ] ending a verse, IJ says that the poet means AlS~in~aboru ; but requiring to make the b movent, he transfers to it the final vowel, as in the phrases h`*aA bakuro and mararotu bibakiro : he should therefore have said AlS~in~aburo ; but regarding the expression as meaning Hiyna hayoji AlS~in~abori , he makes the b to be with kesr, as though he transferred to it the kesreh of the r : this, he adds, is more probable than the opinion that the change is merely one of poetic necessity. (M.) For this last reason, another poet uses the word with teshdeed to the n and r , and with kesr to the b ; saying, nuToEimu Al$~aHoma waAls~adiyfa wanasoqiY A@lo maHoDa fiY AlS~in~abir~i waAlS~ur~aAdi [ We give to eat fat and the hump of the camel, and we give to drink pure milk, in the time of cold wind and chill mist ]. (K.) ― -b2- Also AlS~in~aboru , (M, K,) or ↓ AlS~inaboru , (as in two copies of the S in art. Sbr ,) and Sin~aborN , [without the article Al , occurring in a verse of which the metre requires it to be thus written, with teshdeed to the n ,] (TA,) One, (S,) namely, the second, (M, K,) of the days called A^ay~aAmu AlEajuwzi : (S, M, K: [see EajuwzN :]) AlS~inaboru [or AlS~in~aboru ] and AlS~in~abiru may have the same meaning, [or meanings, or may both be applied to the day above mentioned, for the application of Sin~aborN to that day is certain;] poetic necessity requiring the b to be movent. (S.) ― -b3- Sin~abirN has also two contr. significations, namely, Hot: and cold: accord. to Th, on the authority of IAar. (M.) You say gadaApN Sin~abirN , (M,) or Sin~aborN , (K,) and ↓ SinobirN , (as in a copy of the M,) or Sin~iborN , (K,) A cold morning: (M, K:) and a hot morning. (K.)

definition: A solitary palm-tree, apart from others, (AO, S in art.
sourceDefinition: A solitary palm-tree, apart from others, (AO, S in art. Sbr , and M, A in art. Sbr , and K,) the lower part of which becomes slender, (S and A in art. Sbr ,) and stripped of the external parts [or the stumps of the branches ]: (S ubi suprà:) and a palm-tree slender in its lower part, and bared of the stumps of its branches, and scanty in its fruit; (M, K;) as also ↓ SunobuwrapN : (M:) and a palm-tree that comes forth from the root, or lower part, of another palm-tree, without being planted: (M:) or a little palm-tree that does not grow from its mother-tree: (Ibn-Sim'án:) and the lowest part of a palm-tree, (AHn, Ibn-Sim'án, M, K,) from which the roots branch off: (AHn, M:) and branches that come forth from the lowest part of a palm-tree: (M, K:) or a branch that comes forth from the trunk of a palmtree, not from the ground: this is [said to be] the original signification: (T, TA:) or branches that come forth from the trunk of a palm-tree, not having their roots in the ground: such branches weaken the mother-tree, which is cured by pulling them off: the pl. is SanaAbiyru (IAar) and ↓ SanaAbiru : (T, TA:) and the SanaAbiyr are also called rawaAkiybu and Eiq~aAnN . (Ibn-Sim'án.) ― -b2- Hence, (A,) applied to a man, Solitary; lonely: (IAar:) or solitary, or lonely, without offspring and without brother: (S, A:) or solitary, weak, vile, or ignominious, having no family nor offspring nor assistant: (M, K:) or having no offspring, nor kinsfolk or near relations, nor assistant, whether of strangers or relations: and weak: (IAar:) and mean, or ignoble. (M, K.) See also SanobarN . And A young, or little, (K,) or weak, (TA,) boy, or child. (K, TA.) It was applied as an epithet to Mohammad, by the unbelievers, as also [its dim.] ↓ SunayobiyrN , (M, TA,) or they called him SunobuwrN , (O,) meaning that he had no offspring nor brother, so that, when he should die, his name would be lost; (M, TA;) likening him to a [solitary] palm-tree, of which the lower part had become slender, and the branches few, and which had become dry; (AO;) or to a branch growing from the trunk of a palm-tree. (TA.) -A2- The tube, or pipe, that is in the [ kind of leathern vessel, or bag, for water, called ] A_idaAwap , of iron, (S, M, A, K,) or of lead, (S, M, K,) or brass, (A,) or of other material, (K,) from which one drinks. (S, M, A, K.) ― -b2- The [ aperture called ] mavoEab of a watering-trough or tank [ from which the water runs out ]: (S, M, K:) or the hole, or perforation, thereof, from which the water issues when it is washed. (M, K.) ― -b3- The pipe of copper or brass by which the water runs from one tank to another in a both. (Mgh.) ― -b4- And The mouth of a qanaAp [or water-pipe ]. (M, K.) -A3- Also A cold wind: and a hot wind. (O, K.) See also Sin~aborN . ― -b2- And A calamity, or misfortune. (O, K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, &c.,) aor. yaSuwmu , (Msb,) inf. n. SawomN , and SiyaAmN ; (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K;) and ↓ AiSoTaAma ; (M, K;) He abstained, (Msb, TA,) in an absolute sense: (Msb:) this is the primary signification: (TA:) [or] this is said to be the signification in the proper language of the Arabs: (Msb:) and in the language of the law, (Msb, TA,) he observed a particular kind of abstinence; (Msb;) i. e. (TA) he abstained from food (S, M, K, TA) and drink (M, K, TA) and coïtus: (M, K:) and (S, * M, &c.) by a tropical application, (TA,) (tropical:) from speech: (S, * M, Mgh, Msb, * K, TA:) or SawomN in the proper language of the Arabs signifies a man's abstaining from eating: and by a secondary application, a particular serving of God [ by fasting ]; (Mgh;) [i. e.] the abstaining from eating and drinking and coïtus from daybreak to sunset: (KT:) accord. to Kh, it signifies [properly] the standing without work. (S.) SAm Al$~ahora means SAm fiY Al$~ahori [ He fasted during the month ]: agreeably with what is said in the Kur ii. 181. (TA.) And it is said (S, M) by I'Ab (S) that the saying, in the Kur [xix. 27], (S, M,) A_in~iY na*arotu lilr~aHom`ni SawomFA means (assumed tropical:) [ Verily I have vowed unto the Compassionate ] an abstaining from speech. (S, M, Msb.) One says also, SAm Alfarasu , inf. n. SawomN (S, M) and SiyaAmN , (M,) (assumed tropical:) The horse stood without eating of fodder; (S;) or abstained from the eating of fodder. (M, A, Mgh.) And SAm Eani Als~ayori (tropical:) He abstained from going along, or journeying. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] SAmt Al$~amosu (assumed tropical:) The sun became [ apparently ] stationary [ in the mid-heaven ]: (T, TA:) or attained its full height. (M, TA.) ― -b3- And SAm Aln~ahaAru , (inf. n. SawomN , S,) (tropical:) The day reached its midpoint. (S, M, Mgh, K, TA.) ― -b4- And SAmt Alr~iyHu , (M, TA,) inf. n. SawomN , (S, K,) (tropical:) The wind became still, or calm. (S, M, K, TA.) ― -b5- And SAm AlmaA='u , [inf. n. SiyaAmN (see SulaAqapN ) and probably SawomN also,] (assumed tropical:) The water became still, or motionless; syn. qaAma and daAma . (TA.) ― -b6- And SAm Aln~aEaAmu , (M, K,) inf. n. SawomN , (M,) (tropical:) The ostrich cast forth its dung; (M, K, TA;) and in the same sense the verb is used in relation to the domestic fowl; because each stands still in doing this, or because each becomes tranquil by reason of the passing forth of that which occasions annoyance: and accord. to [some one or more of the copies of] the M, SAm Aln~ahaAru , inf. n. SawomN , The nhAr , by which is here meant the young one of the karawaAn , [or rather of the bustard called HubaAraY ,] cast forth what was in its belly. (TA.) -A2- SAm maniy~atahu i. q. *aAqahaA [ He tasted, or experienced, his death ]. (K.) -A3- And SaAma He (a man) shaded himself by means of the tree called Sawom . (K.)

definition: Abstaining, in an absolute sense: this is said to be the signification in the proper language of the Arabs: and in the language of the law, observing a particular kind of abstinence;
sourceDefinition: Abstaining, in an absolute sense: this is said to be the signification in the proper language of the Arabs: and in the language of the law, observing a particular kind of abstinence; (Msb;) [i. e.] abstaining from food (S, M, K) and drink and coïtus: and, [by a tropical application, (see 1, first sentence,)] (tropical:) from speech: (M, K:) it is applied to a man: (S, M, Msb:) and ↓ SawomaAnu signifies the same, (S, K,) so applied; (S;) as also ↓ SawomN , (M, K,) applied to a man, (M,) and to a woman, and to two men, (TA,) and to a pl. number; (M, K;) being an inf. n. used as an epithet; (TA;) or it is a pl., [or rather quasi-pl. n.,] like zaworN : (M voce DayofN :) or, in the proper language of the Arabs, SaAy^imN signifies abstaining from eating: and by a secondary application, serving God in a particular manner [ by fasting: see again 1, first sentence]: (Mgh:) accord. to AO, it signifies any creature abstaining from food, or (assumed tropical:) from speech, or (assumed tropical:) from going along or journeying: (S, Msb:) pl. sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, K,) inf. n. DaboEN , (TK,) He (a man, S) stretched forth towards him (another man, S) his upper arm ( DaboEahu ), for the purpose of striking. (S, K.) A poet says, walaA SuloHa Hat~aY taDobaEuwanA wanaDobaEaA i. e. [ And there shall be no peace ] until ye stretch forth towards us your upper arms with the swords and we stretch forth our upper arms towards you: or, accord. to AA, until ye stretch forth [ towards us ] your upper arms for the making of peace and the joining of hands [ and we do the same ]. (S.) And one says, DabaEa yadahu A_ilayohi biAls~ayofi , meaning He stretched forth his arm towards him with the sword. (K.) And DabaEa EalaY fulaAnK , (S, * K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) He stretched forth his upper arms for the purpose of uttering an imprecation against such a one: (S, * K, TA:) and hence, DaboEN is metaphorically used to signify (tropical:) the act of supplicating or imprecating; because the person supplicating or imprecating raises his hands and stretches forth his upper arms: and DibaAEN , also, [app. an inf. n. of ↓ DaAbaEa ,] signifies the raising the hands, or arms, in supplication or imprecation. (TA.) And DabaEati Alxayolu , and AlA_ibilu , (S, Msb, K,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. DaboEN (S, K) and DubuwEN and DabaEaAnN , (K,) The horses, and the camels, stretched forth their arms ( A^aDobaAEahaA , S, Msb, K, i. e. A^aEoDaAdahaA , S, Msb) in their going along; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Db~Et , inf. n. taDobiyEN : (S, K:) in [a copy of] the A expl. as meaning mad~ato A^aEonaAqahaA [ stretched forth their necks; but this is probably a mistranscription, for md~t A^aEoDaAdahaA ]: (TA:) DabaEat said of horses is like DabaHat , (K, TA,) which is a dial. var.: (TA:) and DabaEat said of a she-camel, inf. n. DaboEN , signifies the same as ↓ Db~Et , as also ↓ A^aDobaEat , on the authority of IKtt: (TA:) [or,] accord. to As, DaboEN signifies the lifting, (S,) or bending, (TA,) of the hoof, (S, TA,) by a horse, and the lifting of the foot, by a camel, (TA,) towards the arm: (S, TA:) or it signifies the running a pace above that which is termed taqoriyb : (O, K:) or DabaEa said of a camel signifies he hastened, or was quick, (K, TA,) in pace, or going: (TA:) or he went along shaking his arms. (K.) DabaEahu also signifies He (a camel) took him (another camel) by his arms, and threw him down. (L in art. EDd , and TA in the present art.) ― -b2- DabaEuwA lilS~uloHi , (K, TA,) and llomuSaAfaHapi ; (TA;) or DabaEuwA A_ilaY AlS~uloHi ; and DabiEuwA , inf. n. DabaEN ; (Et-Toosee, TA;) They inclined to peace, (Et-Toosee, K, TA,) and the joining of hands; they desired peace, &c. (TA.) ― -b3- DabaEuwA lanaA AlT~ariyqa , (S, K,) or mina AlT~ariyqi , inf. n. DaboEN , (TA,) They gave us a share of the road: (S, K:) so says ISk: (S:) and in like manner one says, *araEuwA lanaATariyqFA . (TA.) And DabaEuwA Al$~aYo'a , (K, TA,) or mina Al$~aYo'i , (TA,) They gave a share of the thing (K, TA) to every one. (TA.) ― -b4- And DabaEa , (K,) inf. n. DaboEN , (TA,) He (a man) acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: (K:) on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed. (TA.) -A2- DabiEat , aor. , inf. n. DabaEN (S, K) and DabaEapN ; (S, * K; [this latter is said in the TA, on the authority of IAar, to have been used by an Arab of the desert in relation to a woman; and is, accord. to the S, app., a simple subst.;]) and ↓ A^aDobaEat , (S, K,) and ↓ AstDbEt ; (K;) She (a camel) desired (S, K) vehemently (S) the stallion. (S, K.)

sourceDefinition: , which the circuiter round the House [of God, i. e. the Kaabeh,] is commanded to perform, (S,) or in the case of the muHorim , (K,) is The putting the [ garment called ] ridaA=' under one's right armpit, and turning back the extremity thereof over his left [ shoulder ], exposing to view his right shoulder [ and arm ] and covering the left; (S, K, TA;) like the man that desires to labour at a thing and prepares himself for doing so; (TA;) thus termed because of exposing to view one of the two upper arms: (S, K:) or the putting one's garment (Mgh, Msb) under his right arm, (Mgh,) or under his right armpit, (Msb,) and throwing [ a portion of ] it upon his left shoulder: (Mgh, Msb:) or the taking the A_izaAr or the burod , and putting the middle of it under one's right armpit, and throwing the extremity thereof upon his left shoulder, over his breast and his back: (IAth, TA:) Alt~aA^ab~uTu and Alt~awa$~uHu likewise signify the same: so says Az: (Msb:) and so says As of the former: (S:) and it is also written AlAiT~ibaAEu . (Thus in the TA in explanation of Alt~aA^ab~uTu .) You say, AiDoTabaEa bivawobihi [ He attired himself with his garment in the manner described above ]. (Mgh, Msb.) And ADTbE Al$~aYo'a He put the thing under his upper arms. (TA. [But accord. to the Mgh, the verb is trans., correctly, only by means of bi .])

sourceDefinition: The EaDud [i. e. upper arm of a human being, and arm of a quadruped], (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) altogether: (K:) or the middle thereof, (Lth, Mgh, O, K,) with its flesh: (O, K:) and the inner side thereof: (Mgh:) or (so in some copies of the K, but in others “ and, ”) the armpit: or the portion, of the upper part of the EaDud , that is between the armpit and the half of the former: (K:) it is of man and of other than man: (TA:) pl. A^aDobaAEN . (S, Msb, K.) One says, A^abad~a DabEayohi , [expl. in art. bd ,] speaking of a man praying. (O, TA.) And A^axa*otu biDaboEaYo fulaAnK falamo A^ufaAriqohu and madadotu biDaboEayohi , meaning I seized the middle of the upper arms of such a one [ and did not relinquish him ]. (Lth, O, TA.) And ja*abahu biDaboEayohi (tropical:) He raised him, or set him up, and rendered his name famous: and in like manner, A^axa*a biDaboEayohi , and mad~a biDaboEayohi . (TA.) -A2- Also Any [ hill such as is termed ] A^akamap that is black and somewhat oblong. (IAar, K.) -A3- *ahaba bihi DaboEFA laboEFA means baATilFA [i. e., app., He took it away with a false pretence; or in play, or sport ]; (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K, TA;) namely, a thing; (O, TA;) laboEFA being an imitative sequent. (TA.) -A4- See also DabuEN . -A5- And see what here next follows.
