(S, M, Msb, K) and , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. lamosN , (S, M, Msb,) He felt it; or touched it; syn. mas~ahu : (IAar, Az, IDrd, El-Fárábee, A, Msb, TA:) or he felt it, or touched it, ( mas~ahu ,) with his hand: (S, Msb, K:) or he put his hand to it: (Msb:) or he felt it with his hand for the purpose of testing it, that he might form a judgment of it; syn. jas~ahu : (M, TA:) and ↓ laAmasahu is syn. with lamasahu , (M, TA,) or maAs~ahu : (A:) lamosN and mas~N both signify the perceiving by means of the exterior of the external skin: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or they are nearly alike: (TA:) [generally, like the English words feeling and touching, respectively:] or the former is, originally, [the feeling ] with the hand for the purpose of knowing the feel ( mas~ ) of a thing: (IDrd, Msb:) or, with the hand, it is the seeking for [or feeling for ] a thing here and there: (Lth, TA:) mulaAmasapN is the same as mumaAs~apN (K, TA) with the hand; as also lamosN : (TA:) or a distinction is to be made between them; for it is said that lamosN is sometimes the feeling, or touching a thing with a thing; and is sometimes [ for ] the knowledge of a thing, though there be no touching ( mas~ ) of substance upon substance; whereas mlAmsp is mostly mutual feeling or touching, &c., being] the act of two. (IAar in TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] lamasahaA , (M, A, Msb, K,) aor. (M) [and , as implied in the K], inf. n. lamosN , (S, M,) (tropical:) Inivit eam; (I'Ab, S, M, A, Msb, K;) scil. mulierem; (A, Msb;) puellam; (K;) as also ↓ laAmasahaA , (M, A, Msb,) inf. n. mulaAmasapN (I'Ab, S, Msb, K) and limaAsN : (I'Ab, Msb:) and (assumed tropical:) he kissed her; by doing which, as well as by the former, one renders necessary the performance of the ablution termed wDw' . ('Abd-Allah Ibn- 'Amr, Ibn-Mes'ood.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] lamasahu , aor. [and ], (A, TA,) inf. n. lamosN , (IDrd, Msb, TA,) (tropical:) He sought, [ as though by feeling, ] or sought for or after, it, namely, a thing, (IDrd, Msb, TA,) in any manner; (IDrd, Msb;) [as, for instance, by asking, or demanding; ] as also ↓ Altmshu , (S, M, A, * K, TA,) [which is more common,] and ↓ tlm~shu : (M, TA:) or this last signifies he sought it, or sought for or after it, repeatedly, or time after time. (S, K, TA.) You say, A^ulomuso liY fulaAnFA (A, TA) (tropical:) Seek thou for me such a one. (TA.) And it is said in the Kur, [lxxii. 8,] relating the words of the jinn, or genii, A_in~aA lamasonaA Als~amaA='a , (K, * TA, *) (tropical:) Verily we sought to reach heaven: or to learn the news thereof: (Bd:) or to hear by stealth what was said therein: (Jel:) or we laboured, or strove, after ( EaAlajonaA ) the secrets of heaven, and sought to hear them by stealth. (K.) And in a trad., bihi EilomFA ↓ mano salaka TariyqFA yalotamisu (tropical:) Whoso pursueth a way whereby he seeketh after knowledge, or science. (TA.) And in another, of 'Áïsheh, EiqodiY ↓ faA@lotamasotu (tropical:) And I sought for my necklace. (TA.) ― -b4- lamasa AlbaSara , aor. , (tropical:) It took away the sight. (A, TA.) And the same, or, accord. to one relation of a trad., ↓ Altmshu , (assumed tropical:) It took away quickly, and destroyed, the sight; said there of certain serpents: or the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) it aimed at the eye with its bite: and lamasa Eayonahu is said to signify [(assumed tropical:) he, or it, put out his eye, ] the same as samala . sourceDefinition: act. part. n. of 1. (Msb, &c.) One says, of a woman who commits adultery, or fornication, or acts viciously, falaAnapu laA tarud~u yada laAmisK , (A, TA,) or laA tamonaEu yada laAmisK , (K,) but the latter is at variance with the written authorities, the former being the phrase commonly known, (TA,) [properly signifying, Such a woman does not repel the hand of a feeler; ] meaning, (tropical:) such a woman commits adultery, or fornication, and acts viciously, (K, TA,) not repelling from herself any one who desires of her that he may lie with her; (TA;) and she is suspected of easiness, or compliance, (K, TA,) towards him who desires of her that he may lie with her: (TA:) or the meaning is, such a woman gives, of her husband's property, what is sought, or demanded, from her; and this is more probably meant in a trad. in which a man is related to have said thus of his wife; because Mohammad directed him to retain her, and did not require him to divorce her. (TA.) The like said of a man, (K,) fulaAnN laA yarud~u yada laAmisK , (A, Msb,) means, (tropical:) Such a man has in him no force of resistance, (A, Msb, K,) nor care of what is sacred, or inviolable. (TA.)

definition: and ↓ muro'N (S, K) and ↓ miro'N (K) A man, or human being;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ muro'N (S, K) and ↓ miro'N (K) A man, or human being; syn. A_inosaAnN : (K:) or a man as opposed to a child or a woman; syn. rajulN . (S, K.) You say maro'N in the nom., maro'FA in the acc., and maro'K in the gen., (S,) agreeably with analogy. (TA.) And some say muro'N in the nom., maro'FA in the acc., and miro'K in the gen.; doubly declining the word. (TA, and some copies of the S.) And ↓ miro' is said to be of the dial. of Hudheyl. It is said that no pl. is formed from mr' ; but marow^uwna occurs as its pl. in the following words of a trad.; A^aHosinuwA A^amolaA'akumo A^ay~uhaA Almurow^uwna [ Amend your manners, O ye men! ]; and in the saying of Ru-beh, A^ayona yuriydu Almrw^wn [ Whither do the men desire to go? ]. (TA.) It forms a dual; mairoA=ni : they say humaA miroA=ni SaAliHaAni [ They are two just men ] (S) in the dial. of Hudheyl. (TA.) It also forms a dim., muraYo'N , fem. murayoy^apN . (S.) ― -b2- The fem. of maro'N is maroA^apN , A woman: [and a wife: ] also written and pronounced marapN . (S, K.) ― -b3- mr' is also written with the conjunctive A : you say A@moraA^N in the nom., A@moraA^F in the acc., and A@moraA^K in the gen.: also, A@moruw^N in the nom., A@moruw^FA in the acc., and A@moruw^K in the gen.: also, A@moruw^N in the nom., A@moraA^F in the acc., and A@moriy^K in the gen.; doubly declining the word. (S, K, TA.) [The last three forms are the most common in classical works: but in ordinary parlance, in the present day, the word is generally pronounced with fet-h to the r in each case. The final ' is also often written without the A or w or Y .] Ks and Fr say, that the word is doubly declined, as to the r and ' , because the final ' is often omitted. (T, TA.) [When the disjunctive A is substituted for the conjunctive, i. e., when the word is immediately preceded by a quiescence, its vowel is kesr: thus you say AimoraA^N &c.; and thus also in the fem. The name of the famous poet AimorauA^u Alqayosi is commonly pronounced Imra-el- Keys and Imr-el-Keys.] ― -b4- The fem. is A@moraA^apN , A woman: [and a wife: ] but with Al you say AlmaroA^apu : AlAimoraA^apu [which is authorized by the K] is also said to be established by usage; but most of the expositors of the Fs reject this; and those who allow it to be correct judge it of weak authority: IO mentions also A@moraApN , with soft A after the r . (TA.) ― -b5- A@morau'N is also used in a fem. sense; (S;) though this is extr.: ex. A_in~ahaA laA@morau'a Sidoq [ Verily she is an excellent woman: see SidoqN ]. (TA.) And A@moraA^apN is used, in a trad., as signifying a perfect woman: laqado tazaw~ajota A@moraA^apF Indeed thou hast married a perfect woman: like as you say fulaAnN rajulN , meaning “ Such a one is a perfect man. ” (TA.) ― -b6- Also, AimoraA^N or A@moruw^N , (S,) or maro'N , (K,) signifies A wolf: (S, K:) or, as Z and others assert, it is tropical in this sense. Yoo says, that the poet means, by A@mrw^ , in the following verse, a wolf: waA^anota A@moruw^N taEoduw EalaY kul~i gir~apK fatuxoTiy^u fiyhaA mar~apF watuSiybu [ And thou art a wolf that assaultest on every occasion of carelessness; and sometimes thou missest therein, and ( sometimes ) thou attainest thine object ]. (TA.) ― -b7- The rel. n. of A@morau'N is maray^iY~N (as in one copy of the S) or muray^iY~N (as in another copy) and A^amariY~N . (S, and El-Ashmoonee and others.) [For the last, Golius, from a copy of the S, gives Aimoray^iY~N : and in one copy of the S, I find it written A^amoray^iY~N : but I have not met with any confirmation of either of these two forms.] maray^iY~N seems to be formed from maro'N ; but is extr.; the analogous form being maroy^iY~N . (TA.)

definition: The heads of bones, (S, Mgh, K,) that are soft, (S,) that may be chewed, (S, K,) or that are sucked: (Mgh:) or soft bones: (A:) or the heads of bones such as the knees and elbows and shoulder-bones: (A'Obeyd:) and the bone within a horn: (Mgh:) sing.
sourceDefinition: The heads of bones, (S, Mgh, K,) that are soft, (S,) that may be chewed, (S, K,) or that are sucked: (Mgh:) or soft bones: (A:) or the heads of bones such as the knees and elbows and shoulder-bones: (A'Obeyd:) and the bone within a horn: (Mgh:) sing. [or rather n. un.] with p : (S, K,) which is also said to signify the prominent part of the shoulder-bone. (TA.) rajulN ha$~u Almu$aA$i rixowu Almagomazi (tropical:) [lit. A man soft, or fragile, in the heads of the bones, flabby where he is felt or pressed, ] denotes dispraise. (TA.) ― -b2- (tropical:) The soul, or spirit; syn. nafosN . (S, K.) You say fulaAnN Tay~ibu Almu$aA$i (tropical:) Such a one is generous in soul, or spirit. (S, A. *) nahi$u Almu$aA$i , applied by Aboo-Dhu-eyb to a horse, means (tropical:) Light, or quick, in spirit, or in the bones, or in the legs. (S, TA.) ― -b3- (tropical:) Natural disposition. (K, TA.) You say, fulaAnN lay~inu Almu$aA$i (tropical:) Such a one is good in natural disposition; one who abstains from coveting. (TA.) ― -b4- (tropical:) Origin. (K, Ibn-'Abbád.) So in the saying Anh lkrym Almu$aA$i (tropical:) Verily he is of generous origin: (Ibn-'Abbád, TA:) or this means (tropical:) verily he is a lord, or chief. (A, TA.) [And similar to this is the saying] ↓ huwa fiY mu$aA$api qawomihi (tropical:) He is among the best of his people. (A, * TA.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Light, sharp, or quick, and who does much service in journeying and at home: (K:) or (assumed tropical:) light in spirit: or (assumed tropical:) one who is a light burden ( xafiyfu Almaw^uwnapi ) to him who consorts with him: or (assumed tropical:) sharp or quick in motions: and, as some say, xafiyfu Alma$aA$i means (assumed tropical:) one who does much service in journeying and at home: so accord. to Ibn-'Abbád. (TA.)

definition: , aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. makorN ; (S, A, Msb, K;) and ↓ Amkr ; (Msb;) He practised deceit, guile, or circumvention; or he practised deceit, guile, or circumvention, desiring to do to another a...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. makorN ; (S, A, Msb, K;) and ↓ Amkr ; (Msb;) He practised deceit, guile, or circumvention; or he practised deceit, guile, or circumvention, desiring to do to another a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, clandestinely, or without his knowing whence it proceeded; syn. xadaEa ; (Msb;) and of the inf. n. xadiyEapN : (S, A, K:) he practised an evasion or elusion, a shift, an artifice, or artful contrivance or device, a machination, a trick, a plot, a stratagem, or an expedient; he plotted; or he exercised art, craft, cunning, or skill, in the management or ordering of affairs, with excel-lent consideration or deliberation, and ability to manage according to his own free will; syn. of the inf. n. A_iHotiyaAlN : (S, TA:) or to this explanation, conveyed by AHtyAl as the syn. of the inf. n., should be added secretly, or privately: (Lth, TA:) makorN is praised or dispraised according to the nature of its object. (El-Basáir.) [For further explanation, see what follows.] ― -b2- It is trans. by means of bi : and also, accord. to Z, by itself: (MF:) [but I know not any instance of its being trans. by itself: except as meaning he plotted a thing: see makora Als~ay~iy^ in the Kur, xxxv. 41, cited voce say~iy^N :] you say makara bihi , (S, A, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, TA,) meaning, He deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him; or he deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him, and desired to do him a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, clandestinely, or without his knowing whence it proceeded: &c.: (S, A, TA:) syn. kaAdahu : or it differs [somewhat] from kAdh , accord. to Aboo-Hilál El-'Askeree: (TA:) some say, that mkr bh signifies as above with the addition of feigning the contrary of his real intentions; which kAdh does not imply: or this latter signifies “ he did him harm, ” or “ mischief; ” and the former, he did him harm, or mischief, clandestinely. (MF, voce kAd .) See art. xdE . ― -b3- makara also signifies He managed with thought, or consideration, or acted with policy, and practised stratagem, in war. (TA.) ― -b4- makara A@ll~`hu and ↓ A^amokara are syn., (IKtt, Msb,) signifying, (tropical:) God recompensed, or requited, for makor [or the practising deceit, &c.]: (Lth, * Msb, TA: *) or makoru A@ll~`hi signifies God's granting a man respite or delay, and enabling him to accomplish his worldly aims [ so as to bring upon himself the punishment due to his evil actions ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or, accord. to IAth, God's causing his trials to befall his enemies, exclusively of his friends: or his taking men by little and little, so that they do not reckon upon it, bestowing upon them renewed favours for acts of obedience which are imagined to be accepted whereas they are rejected. (TA.)

rawSourceText: , aor. , (Msb, TA,) inf. n. makorN ; (S, A, Msb, K;) and ↓ Amkr ; (Msb;) He practised deceit, guile, or circumvention; or he practised deceit, guile, or circumvention, desiring to do to another a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, clandestinely, or without his knowing whence it proceeded; syn. xadaEa ; (Msb;) and of the inf. n. xadiyEapN : (S, A, K:) he practised an evasion or elusion, a shift, an artifice, or artful contrivance or device, a machination, a trick, a plot, a stratagem, or an expedient; he plotted; or he exercised art, craft, cunning, or skill, in the management or ordering of affairs, with excel-lent consideration or deliberation, and ability to manage according to his own free will; syn. of the inf. n. A_iHotiyaAlN : (S, TA:) or to this explanation, conveyed by AHtyAl as the syn. of the inf. n., should be added secretly, or privately: (Lth, TA:) makorN is praised or dispraised according to the nature of its object. (El-Basáir.) [For further explanation, see what follows.] ― -b2- It is trans. by means of bi : and also, accord. to Z, by itself: (MF:) [but I know not any instance of its being trans. by itself: except as meaning he plotted a thing: see makora Als~ay~iy^ in the Kur, xxxv. 41, cited voce say~iy^N :] you say makara bihi , (S, A, TA,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (S, TA,) meaning, He deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him; or he deceived, beguiled, or circumvented, him, and desired to do him a foul, an abominable, or an evil, action, clandestinely, or without his knowing whence it proceeded: &c.: (S, A, TA:) syn. kaAdahu : or it differs [somewhat] from kAdh , accord. to Aboo-Hilál El-'Askeree: (TA:) some say, that mkr bh signifies as above with the addition of feigning the contrary of his real intentions; which kAdh does not imply: or this latter signifies “ he did him harm, ” or “ mischief; ” and the former, he did him harm, or mischief, clandestinely. (MF, voce kAd .) See art. xdE . ― -b3- makara also signifies He managed with thought, or consideration, or acted with policy, and practised stratagem, in war. (TA.) ― -b4- makara A@ll~`hu and ↓ A^amokara are syn., (IKtt, Msb,) signifying, (tropical:) God recompensed, or requited, for makor [or the practising deceit, &c.]: (Lth, * Msb, TA: *) or makoru A@ll~`hi signifies God's granting a man respite or delay, and enabling him to accomplish his worldly aims [ so as to bring upon himself the punishment due to his evil actions ]: (Er-Rághib, TA:) or, accord. to IAth, God's causing his trials to befall his enemies, exclusively of his friends: or his taking men by little and little, so that they do not reckon upon it, bestowing upon them renewed favours for acts of obedience which are imagined to be accepted whereas they are rejected. (TA.)

definition: A certain kind of tree, (Mgh,) or fruit, (Msb, K,) well known;
sourceDefinition: A certain kind of tree, (Mgh,) or fruit, (Msb, K,) well known; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) [the fruit of the banana-tree, or musa paradisiaca; ] i. q. TaloHN [in one of the acceptations of this latter word]: (Msb:) it is lenitive, diuretic, provocative of venery, and augments the spermatic fluid and the phlegm and the yellow bile, and the eating much of it is very oppressive, (K,) for it is slow of digestion: (TA:) the tree grows in the manner of the barodiY~ , [i. e., papyrus, or perhaps other rushes, ] and has a long and broad leaf, which may be three cubits by two cubits, (AHn, Mgh, TA,) the mawoz [i. e., the fruit ] is found, where it grows, throughout the whole year, (AHn, as cited by 'Abd-El-Lateef,) and there may be on one of its racemes from thirty to five hundred fruits; (AHn, Mgh, K, TA;) this is seen in the districts of Makdishoo [between Abyssinia and the country of the Zenj]; (TA;) and when this is the case, the raceme is propped up; (AHn, Mgh;) it rises to the height of the stature of a man, [ and higher, ] and its offsets continually grow around it, every one of them smaller than another; and when it has produced its fruit, the mother-tree is cut down at the foot, and its offset that has attained to its height fructifies, and becomes a mother, the rest remaining its offsets, and thus it continues: whence the saying of Ash'ab, to his son, as related by As, Wherefore dost thou not become like me? to which he answered, Such as I is like the mawozap , which does not attain to a good state until its mother dies. (AHn, TA.) mawozapN is the n. un. (S, Msb.)

sourceDefinition: [ Indian peas; ] a certain grain, well known, (S in art. my$ , and K,) round, smaller than the Him~aS [or chick-pea ], of a tawny colour inclining to greenness; it is in Syria and India; and is sown; (TA;) also called maj~N and xul~arN and zin~N : (TA, art. mj :) it is of moderate temperature; and the mixture made thereof is commended, being beneficial to him who is fevered, and him who is affected with rheum; it is lenitive; and when cooked with vinegar, it is beneficial for purulent pustulous mange or scab; and an external application thereof strengthens feeble limbs: (K:) the word is arabicized [from the Persian maA$o ], or postclassical. (S.) -A2- Utensils and furniture, of the meaner sort, of a house or tent. (IAar, K.) Hence the saying, AlmaA$u xayorN mino laA$a , [in one copy of the K I find laA$K , but the former seems to be the right reading,] meaning, Mean house- hold utensils and furniture are better than nothing; or] what is in the house, or tent, of worthless utensils and furniture, is better than its being empty: (K, TA:) lA$ is here contracted [from laA$aYo'a ] for the sake of its resembling mA$ . (TA.) And xaA$a maA$a and xaA$i maA$i signify the same as maA$N thus used: (K, TA in art. xw$ :) or the refuse, or meanest sort, of people, or of mankind; as in the M. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (as in the L, [but I believe this to be a mistake,]) or , (accord. to the Msb, MS, MF,) inf. n. natojN ; (S;) and ↓ Antj ; (A;) He assisted a she-camel, (S, K, &c.,) [and a mare, see nutijato ,] and a ewe or she-goat (Msb) [or other quadruped], in bringing forth; delivered her of her young one; acting to her as a midwife does to a woman. (T, Msb, &c.) The original form of expression is natajahaA waladFA He assisted her in bringing forth a young one; delivered her of a young one. (Msb.) El-Kumeyt has used the form ↓ Ainotataja in the sense of nataja : but it is not commonly current in Arabic. (TA.) AHn mentions the saying Aln~aAsu ↓ A_i*aA naA='ati Aljabohapu nat~aju wawal~aduwA waA@jotuniYa A^aw~alu AlkamoA^api [ When El-Jebhah (the tenth of the Mansions of the Moon) sets antiheliacally, (for the setting, not the rising, is here meant, and this it did, about the commencement of the era of the Flight, in central Arabia, on the 11th of February,) the people assist their beasts, much, or frequently, in bringing forth, and deliver them, and the first of the truffles are gathered ]. Thus he relates the saying, with teshdeed to the v of ntj , to denote frequency of the act. (L.) ― -b2- nutijato , pass. in form, [but neut. in signification,] inf. n. nitaAjN (S, K, &c.) and tanojN ; (TA;) and ↓ A^unotijato , (K,) also pass. in form; and some say natajato , but this is rare, and not heard by IAar; (TA;) and some, also, say ↓ A^anotajato , (Lth, Kr,) but Az holds this to be a mistake; (TA;) She (a camel, IAar, S, K, &c., and a mare, IAar, and a sheep or goat or other quadruped, Msb) brought forth: (T, Msb, TA:) or one does not say nutijati Al$~aApu unless a man assist at the bringing forth. (Lth.) Thus one suppresses the objective complement of the verb. And one also says tunijati Aln~aAqapu waladFA The she-camel brought forth a young one: and in like manner one says of a ewe or a she-goat: and sometimes, with the same meaning, natajati AlnAqp wldA , in the act. form. (Msb.) One also says AlA_ibilu ↓ tanaAtajati The camels brought forth. (A.) [You say,] nataja Alqawomu , (Lth,) and ↓ A^anotaja , (L,) The people's camels or sheep or goats brought forth: (Lth, L:) or ↓ A^anotajuwA they had pregnant camels bringing forth. (K.) One may also say nutija Alwaladu , meaning The young one of a she-camel &c., [see nutijato , above,] was brought forth, or born. (Msb.) See 4. ― -b3- [Hence,] Alr~iyHu tunotiju Als~aHaAba (tropical:) [ The wind assists the clouds in the discharging of their rain; i. e., draws forth the rain from the clouds. (A, L.) ― -b4- [ nutija It was produced, it resulted, or was a natural consequence. ]

definition: She (a camel, S, and a mare, S, K, or other solid-hoofed animal, Msb,) became pregnant: (T:) and so ↓ natajato , said of a she-camel, (Msb,) or other beast;

definition: and ↓ nadiydN and ↓ nadiydapN A like (S, L, K) of a person or thing: (L:) or a like of a thing by participation of substance;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ nadiydN and ↓ nadiydapN A like (S, L, K) of a person or thing: (L:) or a like of a thing by participation of substance; a more special term than mivolN , which signifies “ a like by participation of anything: ” (the kádee Zekereeyà, MF:) or a thing which does, or may, supply, the place of another thing: (TA:) or a like that is contrary, or opposed, to another thing; (Msb;) that opposes it ( yunaHAd~uhu , i. e., yuxaAlifuhu ,) in its circumstances; (L;) syn. with Did~N and $ibohN : (Akh:) and hence the first is applied to an idol; a thing taken as an object of worship instead of the true God: (L:) pl. of the first, A^anodaAdN ; (L, Msb, K;) and of the second, nudadaA='u ; and of the third, nadaAy^idu . (K.) You say, huwa nid~u fulaAnK , and nadiyduhu , and nadyidatohu , He is the like of such a one: (L:) and hiYa nid~u fulaAnapa , (ISh, L, K,) She is the like of such a female; (ISh, L;) but not nid~u fulaAnK . (ISh, L, K.) You also say huwa nid~iY , and nadiydiY , meaning He is my opponent with respect to the course that I would pursue, contending with me for a different course. (AHeyth, T, L.) -A2- See nad~N .

sourceDefinition: , (S, K, &c.,) aor. , (S, Msb. &c.,) inf. n. na$odN (L, Msb, K) and ni$odapN and ni$odaAnN , (S, M, L, K,) or these two are simple substs., (Msb,) He raised his voice in seeking for, or after, a stray-beast, or beast that had been lost; he called out and inquired respecting it; he cried it: (L:) or he sought for, or after, it: (Lh, A'Obeyd, S, M, L, Msb, K:) and [in like manner] ↓ An$d he asked, or desired, to be directed to it. (M, L, K.) ― -b2- Also, He made known, or gave information of, a stray-beast, or beast that had been lost; (Lh, A'Obeyd, M, L, Msb K;) and so ↓ An$d : (Lh, S, M, IKtt, L, Msb, K:) thus the latter verb [as well as the former] bears two contr. significations. (M, K.) See also naA$idN . ― -b3- na$ada (assumed tropical:) He sought, sought for or after, or desired, a thing. (L.) ― -b4- na$adahu (assumed tropical:) He asked, begged, or besought, him. (L.) ― -b5- nu$ida (assumed tropical:) He was asked, begged, or besought. (S, L.) See 6: and 4. ― -b6- na$adahu , (aor. , L,) inf. n. ni$odapN [and na$odapN (see below)] and ni$odaAnN ; (L;) and ↓ nA$dhu , inf. n. munaA$adapN and ni$aAdN ; (M, L, K;) (tropical:) He adjured him. (M, * L, * K.) ― -b7- na$adahu biA@ll~`hi (tropical:) He adjured him by God; (L, K; *) accord. to most of the grammarians and lexicologists, with a desire of conciliating him. (MF.) ― -b8- na$adahu , (aor. , T, S,) inf. n. na$odN , (tropical:) He said to him na$adotuka A@ll~`ha , (S, L, K,) which signifies I conjure, beg, or beseech, thee by God; (S, A, Mgh, L, Msb, K;) as though thou remindedst him of God, and he remembered; (S, L;) as also A^ano$uduka A@ll~`ha , and biA@ll~`hi , (L,) and A@ll~`ha ↓ naA$adotuka , (A, Mgh, L,) and bAll~`h : (Mgh, L, Msb:) originally, I conjure thee by God, raising my voice: (Et-Towsheeh:) or it signifies I remind thee of God, conjuring; and originally, I beseech of thee by God; the thing for which one conjures being preceded by A_il~aA or what is syn. therewith, [as lam~aA ,] or by an interrogative or imperative or prohibitive: (MF:) or it signifies I remind thee of God, desiring to conciliate thee; as also na$adotuka biA@ll~`hi : (Msb:) or n$dtk All~`h , inf. n. ni$odapN and na$odapN and ni$odaAnN , signifies I adjure thee by God; as also ↓ A^ano$adotuka biA@ll~`hi ; (M, L,) or this latter is erroneous: (Mgh, L:) and so signifies na$odaka A@ll~`ha ; (M, L, K;) in which na$od is said to be originally na$odap , an inf. n. put in the place of the verb, or n$dk All~`h is a phrase of unpremeditated formation, like qaEodaka A@ll~`ha and Eamoraka A@ll~`ha ; or this phrase, which occurs in a trad., may be incorrectly transmitted, and should perhaps be A^ano$uduka A@ll~`ha : (IAth, L:) or na$adahu signifies he said to him na$adotuka biA@ll~`hi wAlr~aHimi [ I conjure thee, or adjure thee, by God and relationship; &c.]: (Lth, T, L:) I beg, or beseech, thee by God, and by relationship, raising my voice. (L.) ― -b9- na$ada He remembered God. (S, L.) ― -b10- He knew, or was acquainted with, a person. (L, K.) ― -b11- na$adahu Eahodahu , aor. , He reminded him of his compact, covenant, engagement, or promise. (Mgh.)

definition: , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) and naZarahu , (M, A, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) and naZarahu , (M, A, Msb, K,) aor. , (M, A, &c.,) and A^anoTuwrN is substituted for A^anoZuru in the dial. of certain Arabs, (IDrd, TS, K,) or, accord. to Lb, in the Bughyetel-Ámál, the w is here added only [by poetic license,] to make the sound of the dammeh full, agreeably with other instances; (TA;) and naZira A_ilayohi , and naZirahu , aor. , (A, K,) the verb being like samiEa accord. to the correct copies of the K, [and so in the A,] but in one copy of the K, like Daraba ; (TA;) inf. n. naZarN , (S, M, A, Msb, K,) and naZorN is allowable, as a contraction of the former, (Lth,) and naZaraAnN (S, K,) and manoZarN (M, A, K) and manoZarapN and tanoZArN , (M, K,) [which last is an intensive form; He looked at, or towards, in order to see, him, or it; ] he considered, or viewed, him or it with his eye; (S, A, K;) with the sight of the eye; (Msb;) [i. e. looked at him or it; ] as also ↓ tnZ~rhu : (K:) and ↓ AntZrhu signifies the same as tnZ~rhu and naZarahu [but app. in another sense, to be mentioned below, and not in the sense explained above, though the latter is implied in the TA; and the same may be meant when it is said that ↓ tnZ~r is syn. with naZara , if this assertion, which I find in the M, have been copied without consideration, and be not confirmed by an example]: (TA:) or naZara A_ilayohi signifies he extended, or stretched, or raised, [or directed, ] his sight towards him or it, whether he saw him or did not see him. (TA.) The usage of Aln~aZarN as relating to the sight is most common with the vulgar, but not with persons of distinction, who use it more in another sense, to be explained below. (TA.) You say, naZara A_ilayohi naZorapF HulowapF [ He looked at him, or towards him, with one sweet look. ] (A.) And naZara fiY AlminoZaAri [ He looked in the mirror ]. (A.) And naZara fiY AlkitaAbi [ He looked into, or inspected, the writing or book ], (A, Msb,) which is for naZara Almakotuwba fiY AlkitaAbi [ he looked at what was written in the writing or book ], or has a different meaning to be explained below. (Msb.) And huwa yanoZuru Hawolahu [lit., He looks around him; meaning,] he looks much. (A.) [See also naZarN below.] ― -b2- naZarati AlA^aroDu , (Sgh, K,) and naZarati AlA^aroDu biEayonK , and biEayonayoni , (A,) (tropical:) The earth, or land, showed (A, Sgh, K) to the eye (Sgh, K) its plants or herbage. (A, Sgh, K.) ― -b3- naZara A_ilayohi (tropical:) It looked towards, meaning faced, him or it. So in the Kur, [vii. 197,] wataraAhumo yanoZuruwna A_ilayoka wahumo laA yuboSiruwna (tropical:) Thou seest them look towards thee, i. e., face thee, but they see not; referring to idols, accord. to A'Obeyd. (TA.) And you say, daAriY yanoZuru A_ilaY daAri fulaAnK (tropical:) My house faces the house of such a one. (S.) And naZara A_ilayoka Aljabalu (tropical:) The mountain faced thee: (A:) as in the following ex.: A_i*aA A^axa*ota fiY Tariyqi ka*aA fanaZara A_ilayoka Aljabalu faxu*o Eano yamiynihi A^awoyasaArihi (tropical:) [ When thou takest such a road, and the mountain faces thee, then take thou the way by the right of it or the left of it. ] (S.) ― -b4- [Hence, perhaps,] naZara Ald~ahoru A_ilaY baniY fulaAnK faA^aholakahumo [app. meaning, (assumed tropical:) Fortune opposed the sons of such a one and destroyed them ]: (S [immediately following there the ex. which immediately precedes it here:]) or naZara A_ilayohimu Ald~ahoru signifies (tropical:) Fortune destroyed them: (M, A:) but (says ISd) I am not certain of this. (M.) ― -b5- Aln~aZaru also signifies (assumed tropical:) The turning the mind in various directions in order to perceive a thing [mentally], and the seeing a thing: and sometimes it means (assumed tropical:) the considering and investigating: [and as a subst., speculation, or intellectual examination: ] and sometimes, (assumed tropical:) the knowledge that results from [ speculation or] investigation. (El-Basáïr.) It is mostly used as relating to the intellect by persons of distinction; and as relating to the sight, most commonly by the vulgar. (TA.) [It is said that] when you say naZarotu A_ilayohi , it means only [ I looked at, or towards, him or it ] with the eye: but when you say naZarotu fiY AlA^amori , it may mean [(assumed tropical:) I looked into, inspected, examined, or investigated, the thing or affair ] by thought and consideration, intellectually, or with the mind: (TA:) [this remark, however, is not altogether correct, as may be seen from what follows: the truth seems to be, that naZarahu and naZaraA_ilayohi may be used in the latter of these two senses, though naZara fiyhi is most common in this sense.] It is said in the Kur, [x. 101,] quli A@noZuruwA maA *aA fiY Als~am`waAti (assumed tropical:) Say, Consider ye what is in the heavens. (TA.) And you say, naZara A_ilayohi He saw it, and (assumed tropical:) thought upon it, and endeavoured to understand it, or to know its result. (TA.) [And He looked to it, or at it, or examined it, intellectually; regarded it; had a view to it. ] And naZara fiyhi (assumed tropical:) He considered it: (TA:) or thought upon it; namely a writing or book; or when such is the object it may have another meaning, explained before; and an affair: and with this is held to accord the saying wafiyhi naZarN , q. v. infrà, voce naZarN : (Msb:) and (tropical:) he though upon it, measuring it, or comparing it. (M, K, TK. In the M and K, only the inf. n., naZara fiY A^amowaAli AlA^ayotaAmi , of the verb in this sense is mentioned.) And fanaTara naZorapF fiY Aln~ujuwmi (assumed tropical:) He considered, or examined, [or estimated, ] the possessions of the orphans, in order to know them. (Msb.) And similar to this is the phrase [in the Kur, xxxvii. 86,] Aln~aZaru , meaning, (assumed tropical:) And he examined the science of the stars: (Msb:) [or he took a mental view of the stars, as if to divine from them.] AlAiEotibaAru when used unrestrictedly by those who treat of scholastic theology means AlAiEotibaAru [(assumed tropical:) The thinking upon a thing, and endeavouring to understand it, or to know its result; or judging of what is hidden from what is apparent; or reasoning from analogy ]. (MF.) ― -b6- naZara bayonahumo , inf. n. naZarN , [app. for naZara fiY maA bayonahumo ,] (assumed tropical:) He judged between them. (K.) ― -b7- naZarato , (TA,) inf. n. naZarN , (assumed tropical:) She practised divination; (K, * TA;) which is a kind of examination with insight and skill. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b8- A^unoZuro liY fulaAnFA (tropical:) [ look thou out for such a one for me; ] seek thou for me such a one. (A, TA.) ― -b9- A^unoZuroniY (assumed tropical:) Listen thou to me. (M, K, TA [in the CK, erroneously, A^unoTironiY .]) The verb [says ISd] has this meaning in the Kur, ii. 98. (M.) ― -b10- A^anaA A^anoZuru A_ilaY A@ll~`hi vum~a A_ilayoka [lit., I look to God, then to thee; meaning,] (tropical:) I look for the bounty of God, then for thy bounty. (A.) ― -b11- naZara A@ll~`hu A_ilayohi (tropical:) God chose him, and compassionated him, pitied him, or regarded him with mercy; because looking at another is indicative of love, and not doing so is indicative of hatred: (IAth:) or (assumed tropical:) God bestowed benefits upon him; poured blessings, or favours, upon him: (El-Basáïr:) and naZara lahumo (tropical:) he compassionated them, and aided them; (Sgh, K;) and simply, he aided them: (K, * TA:) and naZara lahu (assumed tropical:) he accomplished his want, or that which he (another) wanted. (Msb.) -A2- naZarahu is also syn. with ↓ A_itonaZarahu , q. v. ― -b2- Also syn. with A^anoZarahu , q. v. ― -b3- Also naZarahu , (K, TA,) inf. n. naZorN ; (TA;) or ↓ naZ~arahu ; (so in a copy of the M, and in the CK; but from the mention of the inf. n. in the TA, the former seems to be the right reading;) He sold it (a thing, M) with postponement of the payment; he sold it upon credit. (M, * K, * TA.) See also 4. ― -b4- [In these last three acceptations, accord. to the A, the verb is used properly, not tropically.] -A3- nuZira He was, or became, affected by what is termed a naZorap ; (K, TA;) i. e., a stroke of an [ evil ] eye; (TA;) [or of an evil eye cast by a jinnee; ] or a touch, or slight taint of insanity, from the jinn; (K;) or a swoon. (K, TA.)

(TA.) The usage of Aln~aZarN as relating to the sight is most common with the vulgar, but not with persons of distinction, who use it more in another sense, to be explained below. (TA.) You say, naZara A_ilayohi naZorapF HulowapF [ He looked at him, or towards him, with one sweet look. ] (A.) And naZara fiY AlminoZaAri [ He looked in the mirror ]. (A.) And naZara fiY AlkitaAbi [ He looked into, or inspected, the writing or book ], (A, Msb,) which is for naZara Almakotuwba fiY AlkitaAbi [ he looked at what was written in the writing or book ], or has a different meaning to be explained below. (Msb.) And huwa yanoZuru Hawolahu [lit., He looks around him; meaning,] he looks much. (A.) [See also naZarN below.] ― -b2- naZarati AlA^aroDu , (Sgh, K,) and naZarati AlA^aroDu biEayonK , and biEayonayoni , (A,) (tropical:) The earth, or land, showed (A, Sgh, K) to the eye (Sgh, K) its plants or herbage. (A, Sgh, K.) ― -b3- naZara A_ilayohi (tropical:) It looked towards, meaning faced, him or it. So in the Kur, [vii. 197,] wataraAhumo yanoZuruwna A_ilayoka wahumo laA yuboSiruwna (tropical:) Thou seest them look towards thee, i. e., face thee, but they see not; referring to idols, accord. to A'Obeyd. (TA.) And you say, daAriY yanoZuru A_ilaY daAri fulaAnK (tropical:) My house faces the house of such a one. (S.) And naZara A_ilayoka Aljabalu (tropical:) The mountain faced thee: (A:) as in the following ex.: A_i*aA A^axa*ota fiY Tariyqi ka*aA fanaZara A_ilayoka Aljabalu faxu*o Eano yamiynihi A^awoyasaArihi (tropical:) [ When thou takest such a road, and the mountain faces thee, then take thou the way by the right of it or the left of it. ] (S.) ― -b4- [Hence, perhaps,] naZara Ald~ahoru A_ilaY baniY fulaAnK faA^aholakahumo [app. meaning, (assumed tropical:) Fortune opposed the sons of such a one and destroyed them ]: (S [immediately following there the ex. which immediately precedes it here:]) or naZara A_ilayohimu Ald~ahoru signifies (tropical:) Fortune destroyed them: (M, A:) but (says ISd) I am not certain of this. (M.) ― -b5- Aln~aZaru also signifies (assumed tropical:) The turning the mind in various directions in order to perceive a thing [mentally], and the seeing a thing: and sometimes it means (assumed tropical:) the considering and investigating: [and as a subst., speculation, or intellectual examination: ] and sometimes, (assumed tropical:) the knowledge that results from [ speculation or] investigation. (El-Basáïr.) It is mostly used as relating to the intellect by persons of distinction; and as relating to the sight, most commonly by the vulgar. (TA.) [It is said that] when you say naZarotu A_ilayohi , it means only [ I looked at, or towards, him or it ] with the eye: but when you say naZarotu fiY AlA^amori , it may mean [(assumed tropical:) I looked into, inspected, examined, or investigated, the thing or affair ] by thought and consideration, intellectually, or with the mind: (TA:) [this remark, however, is not altogether correct, as may be seen from what follows: the truth seems to be, that naZarahu and naZaraA_ilayohi may be used in the latter of these two senses, though naZara fiyhi is most common in this sense.] It is said in the Kur, [x. 101,] quli A@noZuruwA maA *aA fiY Als~am`waAti (assumed tropical:) Say, Consider ye what is in the heavens. (TA.) And you say, naZara A_ilayohi He saw it, and (assumed tropical:) thought upon it, and endeavoured to understand it, or to know its result. (TA.) (K.) ― -b7- naZarato , (TA,) inf. n. naZarN , (assumed tropical:) She practised divination; (K, * TA;) which is a kind of examination with insight and skill. (TA, from a trad.) ― -b8- A^unoZuro liY fulaAnFA (tropical:) [ look thou out for such a one for me; ] seek thou for me such a one. (A, TA.) ― -b9- A^unoZuroniY (assumed tropical:) Listen thou to me. (M, K, TA [in the CK, erroneously, A^unoTironiY .]) The verb [says ISd] has this meaning in the Kur, ii. 98. (M.) ― -b10- A^anaA A^anoZuru A_ilaY A@ll~`hi vum~a A_ilayoka [lit., I look to God, then to thee; meaning,] (tropical:) I look for the bounty of God, then for thy bounty. definition: , inf. n. munaAZarapN , (T, S, *) (tropical:) He considered, or examined, or investigated, with him a thing or an affair, to see how they should do it: (T, TA:) he investigated, or examined, with him...
sourceDefinition: , inf. n. munaAZarapN , (T, S, *) (tropical:) He considered, or examined, or investigated, with him a thing or an affair, to see how they should do it: (T, TA:) he investigated, or examined, with him a thing, and emulated him, or vied with him, in doing so, each of them adducing his opinion: (TA:) [ he held a discussion with him respecting a thing: ] or naAZarahu is syn. with jaAdalahu : (Msb:) or mnAZrp signifies the examining mentally, or investigating, by two parties, the relation between two things, in order to evince the truth; (KT; and Kull, p. 342;) and sometimes with one's self; but mjAdlp signifies the disputing respecting a question of science for the purpose of convincing the opponent, whether what he says be wrong in itself or not. (Kull.) ― -b2- Also nAZrhu [(tropical:) He, or it, looked towards, or faced, him, or it; was opposite, or corresponded, to him or it. (See naZiyrN .)] ― -b3- (tropical:) He was, or became, like him: (A, K:) or like him in discourse or dialogue. (TA.) ― -b4- jayo$N yunaAZiru A^alofFA (tropical:) An army that is nearly equal to a thousand. (A.) ― -b5- naAZara fulaAnFA bifulaAnK (tropical:) He made, or called, such a one like such a one. (K.) Hence the saying of Ez-Zuhree, (K,) Mohammad Ibn-Shiháb, (TA,) laA tunaAZiro bikitaAbi A@ll~`hi walaA bikalaAmi rasuwli A@ll~`hi , i. e., Thou shalt not call anything like the book of God, nor like the words of the apostle of God: (A'Obeyd, T, K:) or thou shalt not compare anything, nor call anything like, to the book of God, &c.: (A,) or thou shalt not apply [ aught of ] the book of God, nor the words of the apostle of God, as a proverb to a thing that happens: (A'Obeyd, T, K; in which last, we read li$aYo'K ligaraDK , in the place of the right reading, li$aYo'K yaEoriDu : TA:) for, as Ibráheem En-Nakha'ee says, they used to dislike the mentioning a verse of the Kur-án on the occasion of anything happening, of worldly events; (T;) as a person's saying to one who has come at a time desired by the former, (TA,) or to one named Moosà, who has come at a time desired, (K,) jiy^ota EalaY qadarK yaA muwsaY [Thou hast come at a time appointed, O Moosà: (Kur, xx. 42:)] (T, K:) and the like: (T:) but the first explanation is the most probable (TA, as from Az; but I do not find it in the T)

definition: (tropical:) [ He, or it, was made like ].
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) [ He, or it, was made like ]. You say, maA kaAna h`*aA naZiyrFA lih`*aA walaqado A^unoZira bihi (tropical:) [ This was not like this, but has been made like ]. (Msb.) You say, biEotuhu $ayoy^FA faA^anoZarotuhu I sold to him a thing, and granted him a delay. (T.) And a person speaking says to him who hurries him, A^anoZironY A^abotaliEo riyqiY Grant me time to swallow my spittle. (T.) And it is said in the Kur, [xv. 36 and xxxviii. 80,] faA^anoZironiY A_ilaY yawomi yuboEavuwna Then delay me until the day when they shall be raised from the dead. (TA.) See also 8. ― -b2- He sold to him a thing with postponement of the payment; he sold to him a thing upon credit. (M.) See also 1 last signification but one.

definition: A look: a quick look or glance: (T:) pl.
sourceDefinition: A look: a quick look or glance: (T:) pl. naZaraAtN . (A.) Hence the trad., laA tutobiEi Aln~aTorapa Aln~aZorapa faA_in~a laka AlA^uwolaY walayosato laka AlA=xirapu [ Thou shalt not make a look to follow a look; for the former is thine or right, lad the latter is not thine: i. e., when thou hast once looked at anything forbidden, unintentionally, thou shalt not look at it a second time]. (T, TA.) And the saying of a certain wise man, mano lamo taEomalo naZoratuhu lamo yaEomalo lisaAnuhu [ He whose look does not produce an effect, his tongue does not produce an effect ]; (T;) meaning, that he who is not restrained from a fault or offence by being looked at is not restrained by speech. (TA.) ― -b2- A stroke of an [ evil ] eye: (TA:) a stroke of an [ evil ] eye by which one is affected from the jinn's looking at him; (T, S; *) as also safoEapN : (T;) or a touch, or a slight taint or infection of insanity. ( TaAy^ifN ,) from the jinn: or a swoon. (M, K.) ― -b3- An alteration of the body or complexion by emaciation or hunger or travel &c. (S, M, K.) ― -b4- Foulness; ugliness: (AA, TA:) evilness; or badness, of form or appearance; a fault: a defect; an imperfection. (M, K.) ― -b5- (assumed tropical:) Reverence, veneration, awe, or fear, (I Aar, T, K,) ― -b6- (tropical:) Compassion, pity, merry. (I Aar, T, K,)

definition: and ↓ naZuwrapN and ↓ naAZuwrapN and ↓ nuZiyrapN A chief person, whether male or female, to whom one looks.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ naZuwrapN and ↓ naAZuwrapN and ↓ nuZiyrapN A chief person, whether male or female, to whom one looks. (M, K.) definition: (tropical:) Looking to, or facing, another person or thing;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) Looking to, or facing, another person or thing; opposite or corresponding to another person or thing; as also ↓ munaAZirN ; syn. muqaAbilN . (A.) [Hence, naZiyru Als~amoti , and Aln~aZiyru , (tropical:) The nadir; the point opposite to the zenith. ] naZiyruka signifies A^al~a*iY yunaAZiruka , (M,) or Al*Y tunaAZiruhu wayunaAZiruka , (T,) [which I suppose to mean (tropical:) He who looks towards, or faces, thee; who is opposite, or corresponds, to thee; or he towards whom thou lookest, &c., and who looks towards thee, &c.: though susceptible of other interpretations: see 3.] ― -b2- (tropical:) Like; a like; a similar person or thing: (AO, T, S, M, A, K;) equal; an equal: (Msb:) applied to anything: (TA:) as also ↓ niZorN ; (AO, S, K;) like nadiydN and nid~N ; (AO, S;) and ↓ munaAZirN : (K:) fem. naZiyrapN : (T, M, A:) pl. masc., nuZaraA='u : (M, A, Msb, K:) and pl. fem. naZaAy^iru , (T, A,) applied to words and to all things. (T.) You say, fulaAnN naZiyruka (tropical:) Such a one is thy like. (T.) And h`*aA naZiyrN lih`*aA , (T,) or naZiyru h`*aA , (Msb,) (tropical:) This is the like of this, (T,) or the equal of this. (Msb.) And Eadadotu A_ibila fulaAnK naZaAy^ira (tropical:) I counted, or numbered, the camels of such a one in pairs, or two by two; (As, T, K; *) if by looking at their aggregate, you say, EadadotuhaA jamaArFA . (As, T.)

sourceDefinition: act. part. n. of naZara ; Looking; &c.: pl. nuZ~aArN . (Msb.) ― -b2- Aln~aAZiru [ The pupil, or apple, of the eye, the smallest black of the eye, (S, Msb,) in which is [ seen ] what is termed A_inosaAnu AlEayoni , (S,) [ and ] with which the man sees; (Msb;) the black spot in the eye; (M, K;) the clear black spot that is in the middle of the [ main ] black of the eye, with which the looker sees what he sees: or that part of the eye which resembles a mirror, in which, when one faces it, he sees his person: (TA:) or a duct ( Eiroq ) in the nose, wherein is the water of sight: (M, K:) [app. a loose description of the optic nerve: ] or the sight itself: (M, K:) or the eye: (K:) or the eye is called ↓ Aln~aAZirapu ; (S, A; *) the pl. of which is nawaAZiru . (A.) ― -b3- $adiydu Aln~aAZiri , (so in a copy of the M and of the A and in some copies of the K,) or sadiydu Aln~aAZiri , (so in some copies of the K and in the TA,) A man clear of suspicion, who looks with a full gaze: (M, K:) or clear of that with which he is upbraided. (A.) ― -b4- Aln~aAZiraAni Two veins at the two edges of the nose, commencing from the inner angles of the eyes, towards the face. (Zj, in his Khalk el-Insán.) ― -b5- Also, naAZirN (assumed tropical:) A guardian; a keeper; a watcher: (S, Msb:) and, as also ↓ naAZuwrN , i. q. naATuwrN , (K, TA,) [which last is] a word of the Nabathean dialect. (TA.) ― -b6- [The dim. is nuwayoZirN .] You say, EuyayonatiY nuwayoZirapN A_ilaY A@ll~`hi vum~a A_ilayokumo (tropical:) My eye (lit. my little eye ) is looking to God for His bounty, then to you for your bounty. (A.) -A2- In the Kur, [lxxv. 23,] the words A_ilaY rab~ihaA naAZirapN have been explained as signifying Waiting for ( munotaZirapN ) their Lord: but this is a mistake; for the Arabs do not say naTarotu A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i in the sense of A_inotaZarotuhu , but they say naZarotu fulaAnFA in that sense. definition: [ A place in which a thing is looked at ]: a place, or state, in which one likes to be looked at.
sourceDefinition: [ A place in which a thing is looked at ]: a place, or state, in which one likes to be looked at. (T, A, TA.) You say, fulaAnN fiY manoZarK wamasomaEK wafiY riY~K wma$obaEK (tropical:) Such a one is in a state in which he likes to be looked at and listened to [ and in a state in which he is satisfied with drink and food ]. (T, A, TA.) And laqado kunota Eano h`*aA AlmaqaAmi bimanoZarK (tropical:) Thou wast in a state [ in ] which thou likedst [ to be looked at ], away from this place of abode. (T, TA.) ― -b2- The aspect, or outward appearance, of a thing; opposite of maxobarN : (S, art. xbr :) [when used absolutely, a pleasing, or goodly, aspect; or beauty of aspect; as also ↓ manoZarapN : this is implied by the usage of manoZaraAniY~N , q. v., and is well known:] or what one looks at and is pleased by or displeased by; as also ↓ manoZarapN : (M, K:) or the former, a thing that pleases and rejoices the beholder when he looks at it: (T:) and the ↓ latter, the aspect ( manoZar ) of a man when one looks at it and is pleased by it or displeased by it. (T, TA. *) You say, lahu manoZarN HasanN [ He has a goodly aspect ]. (A.) And AimoraA^apN Hasanapu AlmanoZari , and ↓ AlmanoZarapi , [ A woman goodly of aspect. ] (S.) And manoZaruhu xayorN mino maxobarihi [ His aspect is better than his internal state ]. (S.) And A_in~ahu la*uw manoZarK bilaA maxobarK , (T,) and balaA maxobarapK ↓ *uw manoZarapK , (A,) [ Verily he has a pleasing aspect without a pleasing internal state. ]

definition: [The nightingale;
sourceDefinition: [The nightingale; ] a certain bird, (K. TA,) the same that is called EanodaliybN , (S, K, art. Endlb ,) of sweet voice; improperly said in the K to be what is called in Persian hazaAro dasotaAno ; for hzAr itself is Persian, and signifies “ a thousand, ” and daAsotaAno means [as also dasotaAno in that language] “ a tale; ” as though this bird, in the sweetness of its warbling and the pleasantness of its melody, told a thousand tales; being thus called by way of hyperbole and excessive praise: then they contented themselves by employing the word hzAr alone; and the Arabs used it, and prefixed to it the article Al : (TA:) the pl. is hazaAraAtN . (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yahuw$u , inf. n. hawo$N , (S, A, Msb,) It (a company of men) was, or became, in a state of conflict and faction, sedition, discord, or dissension: (Msb:) he, or it, (a number of people,) fell into a bad state, or state of disorder or disturbance; as also hawi$a , like samiEa ; [indicating that its aor. is , and its inf. n. as above;] and ↓ thw~$ : (TA:) it (a company of men, S, A) was, or became, roused, or excited; (A, TA;) in a state of commotion, agitation, convulsion, tumult, or disturbance; (S, A, TA;) and in like manner, ↓ haw~a$a , said of the belly, it was, or became, in a state of commotion, agitation, &c., by reason of leanness: (S:) or hawi$a , like samiEa , [see above,] (K,) aor. , inf. n. hawo$N , (TK,) he (a man, TK) was, or became in a state of commotion, agitation, &c.; or his belly became small, syn. definition: What is gotten by force or theft: (K:) or any wealth, or property, (S,) that is gotten by unlawful means, (JK, S,) such as force and theft and the like: (S:) pl.
sourceDefinition: What is gotten by force or theft: (K:) or any wealth, or property, (S,) that is gotten by unlawful means, (JK, S,) such as force and theft and the like: (S:) pl. of ↓ mahuw$N : (A:) or as though pl. of this latter word, as signifying collected; and mixed, confused, or confounded. (TA.) It is said in a trad., mano A^aSaAba maAlFA mino mahaAwi$a A^a*ohabahu A@ll~`hu fiY nahaAbira [ Whoso getteth wealth, or property, of such as is unlawfully acquired, God will make it to pass away in places of destruction ]: (S:) but this is variously related; some saying ↓ tahaAwi$a ; and some, tahaAwu$K ; and some, nahaAwi$a , with n , which is explained in the K as signifying maZaAlim : the relation given in the S is that which is commonly known by the lexicologists; but all are correct, excepting that tahaAwi$ , with t , and with a kesreh to the w , is disapproved by some of the lexicologists: (TA:) this last word is a contraction of tahaAwiy$u , pl. of ↓ tahowaiA$N , of the measure tafoEaAlN from Alhawo$u , (K, TA,) meaning “ the collecting ”; and “ mixing, ” “ confusing, ” or “ confounding ”: (TA:) or from hu$otu maAlFA HaraAmFA . (Sgh, TA.) A poet says, taA^okulu maAjamaEota mino tahowaA$i [ Thou eatest what thou hast collected of things unlawfully acquired ]. (Sgh, TA.)

definition: ― -b2- raA^ayotuhu waHodahu (S, L, K) I saw him alone.
sourceDefinition: : see 1, and waHiydN . ― -b2- raA^ayotuhu waHodahu (S, L, K) I saw him alone. (S, L.) wHd is here an inf. n., having no dual nor pl. (K.) The Koofees hold it to be in the acc. case as an adv. n. of place: the Basrees, as an inf. n., in every instance; as though thou saidst A^awoHadotuhu biruw^oyatiY A_ibHaAdFA , meaning “ I saw none save him, ” and then substituted wHdh : or, as Abu-l-'Abbás says, it may mean the man's being himself alone; as though thou saidst raA^ayotu rajulFA munofaridFA AinofiraAdFA , and then substituted wHdh . (S.) Or it is in the acc. case as a denotative of state accord. to the Basrees [and the grammarians in general]; not as an inf. n., J being in error in what he says on this matter: (IB, K:) the Basrees hold it to be a noun occupying the place of an inf. n. in the acc. case as a denotative of state; like jaA='a zayodN rakoDFA , meaning raAkiDFA : (IB:) excepting some of them, as Yoo, who holds it to be in the acc. case as an adv. n. of place, for EalaY waHodihi , (IB, K,) like Einodahu : (TA:) and there is a third opinion, that of Hishám; that it is in the acc. case as an inf. n. (L.) Or, (accord. to IAar, L,) it is a noun used as a noun absolutely: (L, K:) so in the dial. of the Benoo-Temeem: (Msb:) you say jalasa waHodahu , and EalaY waHodihi , and jalasaA EalaY waHodi himaA , and waHodayohimaA , and jalasuwA EalaY waHodihimo , [ He sat alone, and they two sat alone, and they sat alone ]. (L, K.) When not preceded by a prefixed n. [or a prep.], it is always in the acc. case: (Lth, L:) you say, laA A_ilaAah A_il~aA A@ll~`hu waHodahu [ There is no deity but God alone ]: and mararotu bizayodK waHodahu [ I passed by Zeyd alone ]: (L:) [excepting in a few cases, such as the phrases] qulonaA h`*aA AlA^amora waHodayonaA [ We two alone said this thing ], and qaAlataAhu waHodayohumaA [ They two women alone said it ]; mentioned by AZ. (L.) You say also, h`*aA EalaY waHodihi , and ↓ EalaY Hidatihi , This is by itself; (L, K;) and humaA EalaY HidatihimaA They two are by themselves: and humo EalaY Hidatihimo They are by themselves: (L:) and A^aEoTi kul~a waAHidK manohumo EalaY Hidatihi Give thou to every one of them by himself; syn. ElY HiyaAlihi . (S.) The p in HidapN is a substitute for the w (S, L) which is cut off from the beginning. (L.) ― -b3- waHodN , (K,) or ↓ waHadN , (L,) A wild animal alone, by itself, or apart from others. (L, K.) ― -b4- waHadN , (K,) or ↓ waHadN , (L,) A man whose lineage and origin are unknown. (Lth, L, K.) ― -b5- waHod is used as the complement of a prefixed n. only in the following phrases: (A'Obeyd, S, L:) huwa nasiyju waHodihi , which is an expression of praise; (S, L, K;) meaning, (tropical:) He is one unequalled; one who has no second: (L:) or he is a man of right judgment: you say also humaA nasiyjaA waHodihimaA , and humo nusajaA='u waHodihimo , and hiYa nasiyjapu waHodihaA , and hun~a nasaAy^iju waHodihin~a : (Lth, L:) [see art. nsj :] it is as though you said nasiyju A_iforaAdK : you put wHdh in the place of an inf. n. in the gen. case: (S:) and rajulu waHodihi , (IAar, L,) and rujayolu waHodihi , (S, L,) [ A man unequalled; who has no second, and a little man (probably meaning the contr.) &c.]: and qariyEu waHodihi A man with whom no one contends in excellence: (Lth, L:) and Euyayoru waHodihi , and juHayo$u waHodihi , which are expressions of dispraise; (S, L, K;) meaning, (tropical:) One who does not consult, nor mix with, any one, and who is contemptible and weak: (Sh, L:) waHod being used in the manner of an inf. n., not being an epithet nor an enunciative so as to be in concordance with the preceding noun, would be more properly in the acc. case; but the Arabs use it in these instances as the complement of a prefixed n.: (Lth, L:) these expressions are indeterminate: for the Arabs say, rub~a nasiyji waHodihi qado raA^ayotu (tropical:) [ Few unequalled men have I seen ]. (Hishám, Fr., L.)

definition: (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ mutawaH~idN (L, K) and ↓ waHadN and ↓ waHidN (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ waHodN (M, L) and ↓ waAHidN (L) A man alone;
sourceDefinition: (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ mutawaH~idN (L, K) and ↓ waHadN and ↓ waHidN (S, L, Msb, K) and ↓ waHodN (M, L) and ↓ waAHidN (L) A man alone; by himself; apart from others; solitary; lonely: (S, M, L, Msb, K;) as also A^aHadN : (M, L, K:) or, accord. to Az, one should not say rajulN A^aHadN , nor dirohamN A^aHadN , nor $aYo'N A^aHadN , though some of the lexicologists assert that A^aHadN is originally waHadN : for A^aHadN is an epithet applied to God alone: (L:) the fem. epithet used in this sense is waHidapN : (K:) and ↓ waAHidN in this sense receives the dual form: and the pl. is wuHodaAnN and A^aHodaAnN and wiHaAdN . sourceDefinition: One; the first of the numbers: (S, L, Msb, K:) syn. [in many cases, which will be shown below,] with A^aHadN : (K:) [and one alone: a single person or thing:] fem. waAHidapN : (L, Msb:) it sometimes receives the dual form; (L, K;) as in the expression A_ilotaqayonaA waAHidayoni [ We met, we being each of us one alone ]; cited from a poet by IAar: or the dual form pertains to it in another sense, explained below, namely “ alone: ” (L:) pl. waAHiduwna (S, L, K) and wuHodaAnN and A^uHodaAnN ; (S, L;) in the last of which, A^ is substituted for w because of the dammeh: (L:) one says, A^anotumo HaY~N waAHidN , and HaY~N waAHiduwna , (Ye are one tribe, L) like as one says $iro*imapN qaliyluwna : (Fr, S, L:) A=HaAdN may also be a pl. of waAHidN [and therefore originally A^awoHaAdN ,] like as A^a$ohaAdN is pl. of $aAhidN . (Th, Msb.) Its proper signification is A thing having no subdivision: and it is secondarily applied to any existing thing; so that there is no number to which it may not be applied as an epithet; wherefore one says, Ea$arapN waAHidapN [ One ten ], and miAy^apN waAHidapN [ One hundred ]. (Er-Rághib.) It is interchangeable for A^aHadN when used as an epithet applied to God; and in certain nouns of number. [See art. A^Hd .] In most cases differing from these two, there is a difference in usage. The latter is used in affirmative phrases as a prefixed noun only, governing the noun which follows it in the gen. case; and is used absolutely in negative phrases: whereas the former is used in affirmative phrases as a prefixed n. and otherwise. (Msb.) [See, again, art. A^aHd .] ― -b2- ↓ lasotu fiY h`*aA AlA^amori bA^awoiHada I am not alone, without a parallel, or watch, in this affair: (S, * L, K: *) or simply, I am not alone in it. (T, L.) The fem. waHodaA='u is not used. (S, L.) ― -b3- A^uHodaAnN , the pl. of ↓ AwHd , is applied by a poet to dogs having no equals or matches. (S, L.) ― -b4- fulaAnN laA waAHida lahu Such a one has no equal, like, parallel, or match. (S, M, L.) ― -b5- Also, One that has no equal; one unequalled. (L.) ― -b6- fulaAnN waAHidu dahorihi Such a person is the unequalled one of his age. (S, L.) And in like manner, (TA,) A^aholi zamaAnihi ↓ fulaAnN A^awoHadu (S, L) Such a person is the unequalled one of the people of his time. (TA.) The pl. of ↓ AwHd [as well as of wAHd in the same sense] is A^uHodaAnN , (originally wuHodaAnN , S) like as suwdaAnN is pl. A^asowadu . (S, L.) ― -b7- waAHidu A^um~ihi [ An unequalled son of his mother ], is an indeterminate expression, like nasiyju waHodihi , q. v. (Hishám, Fr. L.) ― -b8- Also, A man pre-eminent in knowledge or science, or in valour in war, (L, K [in the CK, for baA^os is put nAs ]) or in other qualities; as though having no equal, and thus being alone: (L:) pl. wuHodaAnN and A^uHodAnN . (L, K.) ― -b9- AlwaAHidu and AlA^aHadu (T, L) and ↓ AlA^awoHadu and ↓ AlmutawaH~idu , (M, L, K,) epithets applied to God, The One, the Sole; He whose attribute is unity: (M, L, K:) or the first signifies the One in essence, who has no like nor equal; and the second, the One in attributes, beside whom there is no other: or the first, the One who is not susceptible of division into parts or portions, nor of duplication, and who has no equal nor like: (TL:) or the One who has ever been alone, without companion: (IAth, L:) and there is no being but God to whom the first and second of these epithets are applicable together, or to whom the second is applicable alone. (T, L.) See also A^aHadN , in art. A^Hd . ― -b10- AlA_inosaAnu waAlfarasu waAHidN fiY Aljinosi The human being and the horse are one in genus. And zayod waEamrowN waAHidN fiY Aln~awoEi Zeyd and 'Amr are one in species. (Er-Rághib.) ― -b11- waAHidN Singular, as opposed to plural: pl. wuHodaAnN . (The lexicons, passim.) ― -b12- A^aSoHaAbiY waA^aSoHaAbuka waAHidN [ Thy companions and my companions are one and the same ]. And Aljuluwsu waAlquEuwd waAHidN [ Aljlws and AlqEwd are one and the same ]. (L.) ― -b13- See waHiydN . ― -b14- HaAdiYa Ea$ara , masc., and HaAdiyapa Ea$orapa , fem., Eleventh. In this case, [and in similar instances, as HaAdiY waEi$oruwna Twentyfirst, &c.,] HAdY and HAdyp are formed by transposition from waAHidN and waAHidapN , by putting the first radical letter after the second. [When without the article, it is indecl.: but when rendered determinate by the article, the first word is decl.] You say, huwa HaAdiYa Ea$arahumo [ He is the eleventh of them ]: and Alyawomu AlHaAdiY Ea$ara [ The eleventh day ]: and All~ayolapu AlHaAdiyapu Ea$orapa [ The eleventh night ]. (ISd, L.) [The rules respecting HaAdiYa Ea$ara and its fem. are the same as those respecting vaAliva Ea$ara and its fem., explained in art. vlv , q. v.] ― -b15- biwaAHidapK signifies i. q. faqaTo : and is often used in the sense of Albat~apa . (MF, voce *ur~uwHN .)

definition: One of several hills, such as are called A^akamaAt , separate or remote, one from another: pl.
sourceDefinition: One of several hills, such as are called A^akamaAt , separate or remote, one from another: pl. mawaAHiydu . (L, K.) F remarks, that J is in error in saying, AlmiyHaAdu mina AlwaAHidi kaAlmiEo$aAri mina AlEa$arapi : (TA:) but the meaning of this is, that it denotes one part or portion; like as miEo$aArN signifies one of ten: (L:) [i. e., the former signifies one of several things whereof each is alone, or by itself: ] and the same explanation is given by [several] old authors. (TA.) [In one copy of the S, instead of AlEa$arap , I find AlEu$or ; which affords a good sense, i. e., that myHAd , is syn. with waAHidN ; and may be the true reading.]

definition: The darkness came in upon the people.
sourceDefinition: The darkness came in upon the people. (S, K *.) ― -b2- So in the verse of the Kur. [cxiii. 3,] wamino $ar~i gaAsiqK A_i*aA waqaba And from the mischief of night when it cometh in upon men; (S;) [for other explanations see gaAsiqN in art. gsq .] ― -b3- waqabati Al$~amosu , (inf. n. waqobN and wuquwbN , K,) (tropical:) The sun set: (S, K:) entered its place [of setting.] (S.) ― -b4- waqaba Alqamaru , (inf. n. wuquwbN , TA,) The moon entered upon a state of eclipse; (K;) entered into the cone-shaped shade of the earth. (TA.) ― -b5- waqabato EayonaAhu (and simply waqaba , TA,) His eyes became sunk, or depressed, in his head. (S.) ― -b6- waqaba , aor. yaqibu , inf. n. waqobN and waqiybN , He (a horse) made a sound with his prepuce: [in the S and K, the verb is not mentioned, but only the latter of the two inf. ns., which is explained as signifying “ the sounding of a horse's prepuce: ”] or made a sound by the motion of his penis in its prepuce. (TA.) ― -b7- waqaba , aor. yaqibu , inf. n. waqobN It (a thing) entered: (S:) but it is said in a marginal note in a copy of the S, that the inf. n. is correctly wuquwbN , because the verb is intrans.: accord. to some, it signifies he, or it, entered into a waqobN , q. v.; and in the K, waqobN is given as the inf. n. of the verb in this sense. (TA.) [In the CK, waqot is put by mistake for waqob .] ― -b8- waqaba , [aor. yuqibu ,] inf. n. waqobN and wuquwbN , He, or it, became absent, hidden, or concealed. (K.) ― -b9- waqaba [aor. yaqibu ,] inf. n. waqobN , He, or it, came; approached; advanced. (K.)

definition: , aor. yaliju , inf. n. wuluwjN and lijapN ; and ↓ A_it~alaja ; (S, K;) and ↓ twl~j ; (L;) He, or it, entered. (S, K.) You say walaja Albayota , and ↓ At~ljh , and ↓ twl~jhu , He entered the house....
sourceDefinition: , aor. yaliju , inf. n. wuluwjN and lijapN ; and ↓ A_it~alaja ; (S, K;) and ↓ twl~j ; (L;) He, or it, entered. (S, K.) You say walaja Albayota , and ↓ At~ljh , and ↓ twl~jhu , He entered the house. (L.) And walaja Al$~aYo'u fiY gayrihi The thing entered into another thing. (Msb.) As is said in the S and L, Sb says that walaja has for its inf. n. wuluwjN , which is of one of the measures of the inf. ns. of intrans. verbs, because the meaning [of walajotu Albayota ] is walajotu fiyhi : and it is said in the M, that Sb holds the intermediate particle to be dropped: but Mohammad Ibn-Yezeed holds the verb to be trans. without an intermediate particle. MF observes, that Sb's words appear to make wlj a trans. verb, which no one asserts it to be: that if he mean that it has as its complement a noun in the acc. case as an adverbial noun of place, it is like daxalotu and other intrans. verbs: but if he mean that it governs a simple objective complement, like Darabotu zayodFA , his opinion is not correct. (TA.)
